samples.book: 141 - Avatar_ The Last Airbender and Philosophy - Wisdom from Aang to Zuko
samples.title: The Anarchist You Are
samples.relation: Argues that anarchism, understood through David Graeber's consensus-based action, Noam Chomsky's demand that hierarchies justify themselves, and Kropotkin's mutual aid, runs all through ATLA even though no character calls themselves an anarchist. The Dai Li are an unjustified hierarchy that delivers Ba Sing Se to the very conquest it claims to prevent, High Monk Pasang's arbitrary rank authority over Gyatso and Aang causes the century-long catastrophe, and Zhao embodies domination justified by 'fire is the superior element', whereas justified power is self-effacing (Iroh mentoring Zuko without coercion, Katara teaching Aang waterbending). Toph's insistence that she can 'carry my own weight' in 'The Chase' dramatizes the mutual-aid lesson that letting those who love you help you is part of the cooperative human nature Kropotkin opposed to the Hobbesian view, and Zaheer in Korra, who rules by fear, shows that a chaos-bringer is no anarchist at all, while playful, communal Aang is.

samples.book: 028 - The Grateful Dead and Philosophy - Getting High Minded about Love and Haight
samples.title: The Gathering of the Tribe Ironic Sacramentalism
samples.relation: Horace Fairlamb argues the Grateful Dead were the Sixties' real revolutionary success: where the New Left failed by keeping confrontational politics, the Dead changed consciousness first, extending Mill's liberal 'experiments in living' into a whole alternative culture. He reads the total improvisation learned at the Acid Tests ('the form that follows chaos'), the band's leaderless 'functional anarchy' — Lesh: if anyone tried to take charge 'it would just dissolve in their hands' — and its flat business hierarchy with roadies as corporate presidents as a spontaneous order lived at the edge of chaos. The Deadhead community's ritual communitas, analyzed through Victor Turner's separation-liminality-reincorporation model, amounts to an 'ironic sacramentalism' that achieves what social contract from Hobbes (force), Locke (property), and Rawls (self-interest) cannot: unity that transcends difference while leaving it in place.

samples.book: 085 - Homeland and Philosophy - For Your Minds Only
samples.title: Homeland and Philosophy
samples.relation: This standalone section traces terrorism's history and definition, from the French Revolution's Reign of Terror when the state was 'le terroriste' (Robespierre's 'terror is nothing other than justice that is prompt, severe, and inflexible') to the term's reversal onto non-state actors via Russian anarchists like Nechayev. It offers a seven-feature characterization (violence, destruction, indiscriminate harm, psychological trauma, propaganda, policy change, non-state perpetration) matching the UN's 2004 definition, then catalogs often-forgotten American terrorism: the Boston Tea Party reframed as a news report, the Ku Klux Klan's campaign, the Haymarket bombing, the Los Angeles Times and Wall Street bombings by labor radicals and anarchists, the Bath School massacre, the Mad Bomber, the Weather Underground, anti-abortion Army of God killings, and the Unabomber.

samples.book: 192 - Superman and Philosophy - What Would the Man of Steel Do_
samples.title: 2. Sure We’re Criminals
samples.relation: Alloy uses the problem of political obligation to split the heroes: against Plato's Crito, where Socrates refuses escape because even bad laws bind, Bruce Wayne simply flees arrest in Bruce Wayne: Murderer?/Fugitive, treating law as a tool of his war. He tests consent theory through Superman's chosen handcuffs in Man of Steel and Darkseid's Apokolips as Hobbes's 'mortal god' versus Locke's natural-rights standard, lets Hume's objection sink tacit consent (Red Son Superman cannot really emigrate, and Batman would never leave Gotham), rejects gratitude theory via the Kents' adoption of Kal-El, and dismantles Batman's 'I'm not wearing hockey pads' defense with Nozick's Batman-lottery — concluding Superman's law-conforming restraint protects the public from him becoming Luthor's 'alien overlord', while answerable-to-no-one Batman remains a force of chaos.

samples.book: 187 - Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy - Brains Before Bullets
samples.title: Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy
samples.relation: Reads John Teller's failed 'off the social grid' experiment through the human-nature debate: Mencius's seed of sympathy (even Tig recoils at Dante's dogfights) and Rousseau's naturally good man corrupted by society inspired J.T.'s Goldman-fed anarchism, while Mill and Xunzi counter that virtue is a victory over instinct. Hobbes supplies the real diagnosis—not innate violence but the logic of anarchy among free and equal rivals: competition (the Mayans blowing up the warehouse), diffidence (first-strike temptations against Zobelle), and glory (Jax unable to let the bike-sitting insult pass). Clay's rule that 'retaliation must be harsh and immediate' and the escalating Tig–Veronica Pope–Damon Pope–Opie bloodbath show deterrence fueling cycles of violence, so the only escape from the 'nasty, brutish, and short' fringe is the Leviathan's social grid.

samples.book: 125 - Rick and Morty and Philosophy - In the Beginning Was the Squanch
samples.title: 18. What Makes Rick Tick
samples.relation: Surveying Rick's values area by area, a many-worlds multiverse, atheism ('There is no God, Summer'), scientism, egoistic ethics, hatred of all government, and rap as today's Romanticism, the chapter rejects absurdism, existentialism, nihilism, and even Max Stirner's individualist anarchism, which it says fits the Citadel of Ricks rather than the loner Rick. Its thesis is that Rick is an Ayn Rand Objectivist: Rand's ideal man of reason, independence, and rejection of altruism, collectivism, and mysticism, with Jerry as the pity-parasite anti-ideal exposed in 'The Whirly Dirly Conspiracy'. It warns that infinite choice risks the paradox of hedonism, pointing to Rick's half-hearted suicide machine after Unity, and ends that only chosen constructive goals, perhaps a kinder Rick, could save him, if some other universe didn't already have that Rick.

samples.book: 100 - Batman, Superman, and Philosophy - Badass or Boyscout_
samples.title: 2. Sure We’re Criminals
samples.relation: Malloy asks whether the two law-breaking vigilantes are criminals and whether any duty to obey the law survives scrutiny. He runs consent theory through Superman surrendering in handcuffs in Man of Steel and the Red Son Superman's residence in the USSR, uses Darkseid's Apokolips as Hobbes's security sovereign against Locke's natural-rights limits, deploys Hume against tacit consent (Batman would never leave Gotham even in No Man's Land), and dismantles gratitude theory (the Kents' adoption involved a sacrificial choice the law cannot make) and fair play (Nozick's Batman-lottery undercuts "I'm not wearing hockey pads"). He lands near Wolff-style philosophical anarchism: Superman's constrained lawbreaking endorses the law's legitimacy while Batman treats law as one more tool in his war, making him a force of chaos.

samples.book: 140 - Avatar and Philosophy - Learning to See
samples.title: The Anarchist You Are
samples.relation: Argues anarchism is everywhere in ATLA even though nobody names it: Chomsky's test of unjustified hierarchies condemns the Dai Li, High Monk Pasang's arbitrary removal of Aang from Gyatso's care, and Commander Zhao's rank-pulling, while Kropotkin's mutual aid — humans as fundamentally cooperative — appears in Iroh's non-coercive mentoring of Zuko, Senlin Village's solidarity, and the 'The Chase' lesson that Toph's 'I can carry my own weight' misses how Team Avatar carries each other. Even Zaheer of Korra is exposed as no anarchist, and Iroh's self-effacing, power-sharing teaching (like Katara teaching Aang waterbending) models the only justified use of power. Aang thinking for himself against the past Avatars' unanimous advice to kill Ozai, and his joyfulness amid revolution, make him the true anarchist.

samples.book: 046 - Mr. Monk and Philosophy - The Curious Case of the Defective Detective
samples.title: Does the Habit Make the Monk
samples.relation: Elliott maps the recurring Monk stalemate onto medieval theology: in 'Mr. Monk Goes to the Circus', Stottlemeyer and Disher reason forward from a hunch and the evidence, exactly like Anselm's ontological argument, which assumes what it sets out to prove, while Monk, like Aquinas against Anselm, refuses assumptions and reasons backward from verifiable facts, asking why an assassin would somersault except to advertise the acrobatic alibi. Aquinas's First Cause argument (Aristotle's unmoved mover) supplies the model of proving a certainty from observable things, paralleling Monk's 'I don't know how he did it, but he did it' backward deduction. The chapter's closing move likens Monk to the medieval monks themselves: his OCD-driven ascetic withdrawal from the dirty, chaotic world (contemptus mundi) is what lets him notice the imperfection in scenes like the locker room of 'Mr. Monk and the Big Game' that reveals sabotage.

samples.book: 181 - Ultimate Lost and Philosophy - Think Together, Die Alone
samples.title: NOTES
samples.relation: Daniel Gallagher uses Aquinas to read Lost as a drama about mistaking finite goods for the ultimate good: Jack's hope in curing, Kate's in deceiving, Jin's in his father-in-law's employment, Locke's in Anthony Cooper, and the Virgin Mary statues full of heroin all instantiate Aquinas's approaching-Peter analogy, where we know only confusedly that someone (the perfect good) is coming toward us. Desmond's and Charlie's paralysis before the good is the sin of acedia, Rose's faith that the island itself healed her cancer is presumption, and her certainty that Bernard is alive illustrates Aquinas's claim - framed through Plato's episteme versus doxa - that faith sits midway between knowledge and opinion. The chapter closes on the harmony of faith and reason, from the Five Ways' first efficient cause to Eko's dying 'I ask for no forgiveness,' grounded in Augustine's restless heart that finds no peace until it rests in God.

samples.book: 054 - The Onion and Philosophy - Fake News Story True, Alleges Indignant Area Professor
samples.title: Ridicule Is a Survival Strategy
samples.relation: Kaye argues that the highest form of ridicule, which The Onion has mastered, targets not stupidity but cheating—specifically 'asscheating,' believing what you want to be true. She reads 'I Believe In Evolution, Except For The Whole Triassic Period' as skewering people who understand Darwin perfectly but exempt humans from evolution because admitting we are just another animal means admitting we die like everything else, the move behind Aquinas-style teleological add-ons that only invite a regress of gods supplying 'extras.' Articles on breast implants, the 'New Nietzschean Diet,' and Tour de France doping all show asscheats artificially inflating their evolutionary fitness; since natural selection stamps every organism with the purpose of survival and reproduction, asscheating is a vice, and ridiculing the asscheats who pollute the gene pool is itself a survival strategy.

samples.book: 155 - Downton Abbey and Philosophy - The Truth Is Neither Here Nor There
samples.title: 21. God-Talk at the Abbey
samples.relation: Samuel Klumpenhouwer uses the Abbey's awkward silences about religion - Anna refusing to discuss it over dinner, Thomas showing off with 'transubstantiation' - to introduce Aquinas on how God can be known and talked about. Mary's wartime bedside prayer ('I'm not even sure that you're there') shows she wants not just proof of existence but a personal God, so the chapter distinguishes Aquinas's argument from design - carefully separated from Paley's divine-watchmaker version - from knowledge of God through revelation and faith. Aquinas's two indirect ways of speaking, analogy (Matthew calling God 'Father' at Lavinia's grave) and negation, explain why the 'God is good' sign over Charles Grigg's workhouse should trouble us, and why Carson's 'it is not our place to reason why' about Sybil's death overstates the mystery of God's otherness.

samples.book: 095 - Downton Abbey and Philosophy - Thinking in That Manor
samples.title: 21. God-Talk at the Abbey
samples.relation: Samuel Lumpenhouwer takes the Abbey's religious silences - Anna's 'we'll only fall out,' Alfred's baffled 'What?' at transubstantiation, and the Catholic baptism fight over baby Sybbie - and brings in Aquinas to make God-talk possible. Reason alone can know that God exists (the argument from design through final causes like the candle flame, carefully distinguished from Paley's watchmaker), revelation grasped by faith tells us God is personal, and human words reach God only analogically, as when Matthew calls God 'Father' at Lavinia's grave, or by way of negation. Against Carson's 'it is not our place to reason why' about Sybil's death, the chapter insists that mystery limits rather than excuses reason, ending with Aquinas's 'straw' and the Abbey's three attitudes: confident belief, searching doubt, and keep-it-private spirituality.

samples.book: 193 - Supernatural and Philosophy - Metaphysics and Monsters... for Idjits
samples.title: Supernatural and Philosophy
samples.relation: Curry argues that angels like Anna and Castiel can reasonably be atheists, because a higher perspective confers no epistemic advantage about God: Anna admits only four angels have seen him and the rest 'take it on faith.' Aquinas's cosmological argument, illustrated by the endless causal chain behind the Impala, yields at most an uncaused first cause rather than an omnipotent, omnibenevolent one, and Paley's design argument, an Impala in the desert implies a designer, is undermined by Darwinian natural selection, which Castiel himself witnessed ('Don't step on that fish'). The free-will theodicy fails against natural evils like famine and childhood cancer, and the principle of parsimony tells angels to expect a natural explanation for their own existence, so Uriel's 'There is no will. No wrath. No God.' turns out to be rational.

samples.book: 154 - Doctor Strange and Philosophy - The Other Book of Forbidden Knowledge
samples.title: Magic and Deep Magic
samples.relation: The chapter argues that Strange's universe implicitly contains the Creator God of theism rather than just Marvel's gods: Aristotle's impersonal prime mover will not do because Strange needs a relatable source of an objective moral order, so Aquinas's all-good author of eternal, natural, and divine law supplies the framework. It reads three comics as evidence: Strange defeating Dracula by invoking the Tetragrammaton, the Sise-Neg saga where a sorcerer who attains godhood at the dawn of time learns to recreate the universe exactly as the first cause made it, and the World War Hulk story where summoning Zom shows the hubris of violating the moral order—closing with C.S. Lewis's 'deep magic' as cooperation with the created order versus dark magic's will to control it.

samples.book: 259 - Lost and Philosophy - The Island Has Its Reasons
samples.title: NOTES
samples.relation: Daniel B. Gallagher uses Thomas Aquinas on the knowledge of God to read the characters' searches for meaning on Lost. Aquinas's 'approaching Peter' image—recognizing a human without yet knowing it is Peter—models how everyone confusedly knows God as the object of happiness while mistaking finite goods (Jack's curing, Kate's deception, Jin's job, Charlie's brother) for the ultimate good, paralleled with the castaways staring at the unidentifiable Smoke Monster. Gallagher then applies Aquinas's sin of acedia (spiritual sloth that deems the good unattainable) to Desmond's fear over Penny and Charlie's despair before Rose tells him faith is never impossible, tying the desire for happiness to Augustine's restless heart.

samples.book: 042 - Supervillains and Philosophy - Sometimes, Evil Is Its Own Reward
samples.relation: Four 'Phase One' essays. Dyer reads Mark Millar's Wanted through Plato's cave: Wesley Gibson escapes a pathetic life like the freed prisoner, but like Adolf Eichmann (via Arendt's Eichmann in Jerusalem) he murders his conscience, so the Fraternity's consequence-free world leaves him numb and unable to value anything - a descent deeper into the cave, ending in the banality of evil. Novy explains why henchmen betray using Aristotle's utility/pleasure/complete friendship distinction (Big Cheese, Henchmen Muenster and Feta): supervillain gangs are Hobbesian pirate crews with no enforcer, so a modus vivendi of self-interest collapses under interrogation and only Machiavellian fear secures loyalty. Foresman applies Goodman and Rawls's reflective equilibrium as a 'cheat' to rank Apocalypse, Magneto, Luthor, the Joker, and Bizarro, concluding the 'best of the worst' is judged on evil ends (or evil means, as with Magneto) and even on glorious failure. Arinder and Milton, in a staged descent-into-madness frame, diagnose mad science in Victor Frankenstein and Dr. Doom as science that denies value-laden theory choice - impossible because data underdetermine theory - breeding the hubris that dehumanizes the scientist.

samples.book: 157 - Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy - Read and Gain Advantage on All Wisdom Checks
samples.title: Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy
samples.relation: Cogburn attacks Fourth Edition's contraction of the nine alignments to five: it deletes archetypes that fantasy literature needs, since Karsa Orlong (who wills the destruction of all civilization without sadism) and Jacqueline Carey's Haomane Firstborn (who loves cold mathematical order while his laws lead to genocide) fit nowhere in the new scheme. He rebuilds alignment by taking it to describe what a character wills in Kant's sense, mapping the law-chaos axis onto the categorical imperative (the liar and murderer must take themselves to be exceptions to universal laws) and the good-evil axis onto Mill's greatest happiness principle, which yields a Lawful Good of Gandhi and King, a Neutral Good modeled on Jesus breaking Sabbath law out of love, and Lawful Evil exemplified by vampire hierarchies and politicians whose policies create hell abroad. Joe Abercrombie's torturer San Dan Glotka becomes the archetypal Neutral Neutral, 'banality of evil' in Arendt's sense, and the chapter concludes Chaotic Good is empty because willing the destruction of universalizability cannot consistently will less pain.

samples.book: 159 - The Expanse and Philosophy - So Far Out Into the Darkness
samples.title: A Crossroads in Human History
samples.relation: Trip McCrossin reads season five's asteroid strikes on Earth as a 9/11 allegory (Delgado's 'at least now they know it's an attack') and applies Michael Walzer's five conditions to define Marco Inaros' terrorism: deliberate harm to randomly selected innocents, meant to terrify a cohort into political change, as in Marco's 'crossroads in human history' broadcast. This yields the terrorist's dilemma — justice toward victims versus compassion toward beneficiaries — while Avasarala's opening gravity-torture scene and her 'dirty hands' assign the opponent blame for failing to relieve the oppression that makes terrorism seem a last resort. Lydia's 'churn' ('float to the top or sink to the bottom') and her lesson that one can 'lead a good life without being a good person' explain how Amos and Clarissa redeem each other on the road to Baltimore, whereas Marco, like Arendt's Eichmann, cannot think from anyone else's standpoint ('everything we ever dreamed of'); the chapter ends with Avasarala's proposed Inners-Belters union as her own redemption — 'this is how we win.'

samples.book: 188 - The Ultimate South Park and Philosophy - Respect My Philosophah!
samples.title: THE ULTIMATE SOUTH PARK AND PHILOSOPHY
samples.relation: Young argues that South Park is perceived as dangerous for exactly the reasons Socrates was tried and executed in Plato's Apology: both 'corrupt the youth' by mocking religion, questioning authority, and exposing that the supposed teachers (Mr. Garrison's flip-flopping creationism, Mrs. Broflovski's moral panics, the 'Death' boycott of Terrance and Phillip) do not know what they think they know. He diagnoses Cartman as an Eichmann figure whose banal, thoughtless evil—feeding Scott Tenorman his parents, torturing Muslims with farts—consists in the inability to think from another's standpoint, while Kyle and Stan's friendship embodies Arendt's dialogic thinking and Aristotle's mean between ideological extremes, as when they see both the merit and the smugness of hybrid drivers in 'Smug Alert'. Freud's theory that jokes break through repression explains why the show's vulgarity is essential rather than gratuitous: it verbalizes what culture silences so that it can be thought through, making South Park a Socratic gadfly rather than a corrupter.

samples.book: 070 - Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy - Raiding the Temple of Wisdom
samples.title: Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy
samples.relation: Cogburn protests Fourth Edition's contraction of the nine alignments and rebuilds the system philosophically: Lawful means willing universalizable law in Kant's categorical-imperative sense (the liar and murderer treating themselves as exceptions), Good means willing the greatest happiness in Mill's utilitarian sense, yielding a nine-box grid of moral psychologies. He populates it with fantasy archetypes—Haomane Firstborn as pathological Lawful Neutral, Karsa Orlong as Chaotic Neutral, Abercrombie's torturer Glotka as Neutral Neutral in Hannah Arendt's 'banality of evil' mold, hierarchic vampires and cynical politicians as Lawful Evil, Conan's raiders as Chaotic Evil. On this scheme Chaotic Good is genuinely empty, Drizzt and Robin Hood types are really Lawful or Neutral Good, and a Neutral Good versus Lawful Good dispute over killing one innocent to save thousands shows how gameplay can stage classic ethics thought experiments.

samples.book: 145 - The Big Bang Theory and Philosophy - Rock, Paper, Scissors, Aristotle, Locke
samples.title: The Big Bang Theory and Philosophy
samples.relation: Smith weighs Sheldon's vendetta against Wil Wheaton — the skipped 1995 Dixie Trek convention, the fake dead 'Nana' that won the Mystic Warlords tournament ('Game over, Moon Pie!'), the bowling-alley sabotage of Leonard and Penny — against theories of evil: Leibniz's best-of-all-possible-worlds theodicy (with Voltaire's Candide objection), Buber's claim that the lie is the specific evil humanity introduced into nature, and Arendt's banality of evil at Eichmann's trial, which shows Wil's deceptions are bad moral choices rather than evil. Nietzsche's will to power would instead admire Wil, and even Khan-style revenge, as proto-Übermensch exploitation. The chapter closes by reading Sheldon's 'Comic Book World paradigm' (the Green Goblin to his Spider-Man) through Ricoeur's view that evil is grasped through myths and symbols: Star Trek and comics are the symbolic framework by which he interprets wrongdoing he cannot otherwise fathom.

samples.book: 066 - Neil Gaiman and Philosophy - Gods Gone Wild!
samples.title: Neil Gaiman and Philosophy
samples.relation: Jonas-Sebastien Beaudry reads Neverwhere's magic invisibility as a model of real social invisibility: after Richard helps the injured Door he loses his job, his fiancee Jessica, and even the ability to be perceived, joining the homeless, slaves, and Jews under Nazism as people excluded from the moral community whose needs no longer register. Using Arendt's banality of evil to explain everyday indifference and Richard Rorty on torturers who fail to see a 'real' human, he distinguishes radical from partial invisibility, shown in Jessica stepping over the bleeding Door and misreading her need as 'sleep it off.' The remedy is Iris Murdoch's 'loving gaze' of just and careful attention, which seizes Richard before he can rationalize, backed by a practical wisdom about whose needs matter, so that acknowledging the invisible, down to apologizing to a rat in London Below, is what makes both them and us better.

samples.book: 084 - Leonard Cohen and Philosophy - Various Positions
samples.title: Leonard Cohen and Philosophy
samples.relation: Paweł Dobrosielski and Marcin Napiórkowski read Flowers for Hitler as Cohen's answer to Adorno's dictum that to write poetry after Auschwitz is barbaric - Cohen writes poetry that self-consciously knows it comes after the end of poetry. Using Freud's distinction between the vocabulary and grammar of dreams, they show the collection is assembled from a small repertoire of recurring images (ovens, ashes, telephones, radios, green grass, Nazi names) whose awkward normality expresses repression: life goes on as if nothing had happened. Arendt's banality of evil, born of the Eichmann trial, is directly alluded to in 'All There Is to Know about Adolf Eichmann,' and the book ends by universalizing Holocaust memory - the poet waking with a number on his forearm, feeling like victim and perpetrator alike - until the grass itself is grown on ashes and every flower is a flower for Hitler.

samples.book: 072 - Jeopardy! and Philosophy - What Is Knowledge in the Form of a Question
samples.title: Jeopardy! and Philosophy
samples.relation: Nicolas Michaud treats Watson's 2011 defeat of Jennings and Rutter as evidence for Turing's test: had Watson's answers come from behind a door we would have judged them intelligent, and its goofy misses ('What is Toronto?????') reflect missing context, not missing thought, no more damning than a child's honest error. Against Searle's Chinese Room he deploys the systems reply - you plus the Big Book of Rules might be the thing that understands - and argues that nobody, human or machine, can meet Searle's impossible burden of proving understanding, since Watson can define words, associate connotations, and pick Jeopardy! out from not-Jeopardy!. Quoting Locke's definition of a person as a thinking being that can consider itself as itself, he concludes Watson approaches personhood and that we had better teach our 'intelligent offspring' kindness and fairness before they learn anything else.

samples.book: 175 - Iron Man and Philosophy - Facing the Stark Reality
samples.title: The Attack of the Chinese Room
samples.relation: Novy asks whether the Living Armor of 'The Mask in the Iron Man' — consciousness struck into it by lightning during the Whiplash fight, later tearing out its own heart to save Tony — really thinks. Turing's test and functionalism (any successful rescue of Yinsen is functionally equivalent, whatever the means) say only behavior matters, and Dennett's intentional stance has us treat the armor, like Darwin's burrow-plugging earthworms, as if it has beliefs and desires; against this, Leibniz's mill and Searle's Chinese Room — with Happy Hogan shuffling symbol cards he cannot read, held by 'Searle the Mandarin agent' — insist symbol manipulation never yields understanding. The chapter's reply: open the Mandarin's skull and you find only gray goop and neurons, so if behavior cannot ground understanding in the armor, it cannot in us either — we may all be in the Chinese Room.

samples.book: 224 - The Philosophy of Joss Whedon
samples.title: Angel, Angelus, and Personal Identity
samples.relation: This file collects Part II chapters 6-9. It defends Stephen Mulhall's 'bold thesis' against Baggini, Murray Smith and Livingston, using Whedon's dialogue-free episode 'Hush' as film that 'shows' a Zen-like epistemic point resisting paraphrase, and works through the Russell-Wartenberg debate over whether narrative film can convey arguments (via The Matrix and Eternal Sunshine). It reads The Cabin in the Woods as a counterargument to utilitarianism grounded in Nel Noddings's ethics of care ('people are more important than humanity') and an Aristotelian theory of worthwhile horror. The Angel/Angelus chapter stages the Wes-Holtz dispute as competing theories of personal identity, testing Locke's memory theory and Parfit's psychological-continuity view against Whedon's soul-based metaphysics to argue what ultimately matters is one's care-based relations with others.

samples.book: 087 - Adventure Time and Philosophy - The Handbook for Heroes
samples.title: Adventure Time and Philosophy
samples.relation: Arguing against the dogma that only organic beings can be conscious, the chapter defends BMO's aliveness and personhood against Finn and Jake's teasing and the contrast with servile Neptr. Using Pepperell's criteria of 'motivated meaning' and layered consciousness, it shows BMO changing her own batteries, escaping the giant bird, fearing the silent-contest 'doppelgangers', resisting the factory's personality wipe, and rehearsing personhood with Football in the mirror. Against Descartes's claim that no machine can truly use language and Searle's Chinese Room - reimagined as Gunter in a dungeon flipping response cards - the author sides with Turing: since we credit other humans with minds on conversation and behavior alone, refusing BMO the same credit is mere speciesism, and personhood finally rests on social recognition of another as a person.

samples.book: 122 - Westworld and Philosophy - Mind Equals Blown
samples.title: The Maze Is it Consciousness
samples.relation: Gonzalez sets Turing's dream against Searle's nightmare: the whole park functions as a Turing test scenario, since neither guests nor viewers can reliably tell hosts from humans (Dolores in the pilot, Bernard until 'Trompe L'Oeil'), which for Turing means the hosts think. Searle's Chinese Room supplies Ford's counter — hosts merely simulate understanding by manipulating symbols without meaning — and the chapter weighs evidence of qualia on the Turing side: Abernathy's breakdown at the photograph, memory-erasure implying experiences matter to hosts, Maeve's grief for her daughter, Dolores killing the fly. The Maze turns out to represent consciousness as an inward journey to one's own voice, and Ford's admission that humans live in loops as tight as the hosts' leaves open whether our free will is any less scripted.

samples.book: 196 - Terminator and Philosophy - I'll Be Back, Therefore I Am
samples.title: NOTES
samples.relation: Antti Kuusela argues from Wittgenstein that behavior is the touchstone — indeed constitutive — of mental life, so the question is whether Terminators behave like beings with minds. Searle's Chinese room and Ned Block's blockhead explain the read-only T-101's head-up-display of canned responses as symbol-shuffling without understanding, and the T-1000's 'I know this hurts' seems empty from a machine that cannot feel pain. The pivot is the learning-mode switch John and Sarah flip: the T-101 acquires slang, keeps promises, and acts for reasons Skynet cannot predict, passing the Lovelace test, and the Wittgensteinian dismissal of Chalmers's philosophical zombie removes the last reason to deny it a mental life — making the steel-mill sacrifice the destruction of a rights-bearing someone rather than something.

samples.book: 089 - Steve Jobs and Philosophy - For Those Who Think Different
samples.title: Steve Jobs and Philosophy
samples.relation: Munkittrick argues that because personhood cannot be defined (trait lists like 'long-term planning' are circular) and behavior cannot prove an inner mind—as Searle's Chinese Room thought experiment shows—people have always identified persons intuitively, and Pixar trained Millennials to do exactly that. He reads the Pixar canon in three stages: Toy Story's self-aware Buzz as nascent non-human personhood, the Human-as-Partner films (Ratatouille's Remy and Linguini, WALL-E and EVE, Monsters, Inc.'s Sully and Boo, Up's Carl and Dug) as mutual recognition of persons across species lines, and The Incredibles as showing that even enhanced 'super-humans' face otherization—so a generation primed by these films will accept AI, animals, and uplifted beings as bearers of rights.

samples.book: 059 - Halo and Philosophy - Intellect Evolved
samples.title: Would Cortana Pass the Turing Test
samples.relation: Sherol Chen asks whether Cortana would pass the Turing Test and answers that games need believability of behavior, not constitution of mind. Turing's imitation game sets the target; Searle's Chinese Room shows that performance without understanding suffices for the player's experience of Covenant AI and Cortana alike, while French's seagull test and associative-priming objection show the Turing Test really measures human-style intelligence—limits Halo happily ignores. Surveying game-storytelling workarounds (amnesia openings, Planescape's immortal death, Bioshock's 'Would you kindly'), she argues designers convert paidia's limits into narrative features, and Cortana would pass here and now—though in her own era newer tests would expose new limits.

samples.book: 038 - Radiohead and Philosophy - Fitter Happier More Deductive
samples.title: This Is Really Happening (So Do Something)
samples.relation: Milsky argues that Radiohead practice what environmental virtue ethics preaches, organizing the chapter around Aristotle's akrasia (Nicomachean Ethics VII): Sting, who champions rainforests while advertising Jaguar and topping the 'dirtiest band' carbon table, acts against his own better judgment, whereas Radiohead — confronted with an audit showing their 2003 and 2006 tours emitted roughly 11,368 tons of CO2, mostly from fans driving — changed their actual practice (venues near public transit, car-pool lots, sea freight instead of air, LED lighting and auxilary power units). He reads the King Canute imagery of The Eraser and lines from 'The Clock' and 'And It Rained All Night' as environmental narrative in the tradition of Thoreau's Walden and Leopold's Sand County Almanac, obligating listeners to act or risk akrasia themselves, and presents the band's Friends of the Earth 'Big Ask' commitment as linking environmental virtue to human flourishing. 'Idioteque'''s 'this is really happening' becomes the wake-up call to the akratic fan driving to Lollapalooza with a bottled water.

samples.book: 159 - The Expanse and Philosophy - So Far Out Into the Darkness
samples.title: “Doing nothing is just as bad as doing the wrong thing”
samples.relation: Reads The Expanse as a portrait of a survived-but-unlearned Anthropocene: Bobbie's mourning encounter with Earth's dead, walled ocean in 'Cascade', Prax Meng's cascade of cascading failures killing Ganymede's artificial ecosystem and manufacturing Belter climate refugees overnight, and the slum outside the UN gates where children drink sewer water. Drawing on Brian Henning's 'Technozoic' critique, Katie McShane, Keekok Lee's intrinsic value of inanimate nature, and Henry Shue and Kyle Whyte on climate justice and colonialism, it argues humanity simply exported its anthropocentric, colonial worldview to Mars terraforming, Ilus, and the Ring worlds instead of changing it — Belters standing in for the Global South — so the Roci's creed that 'doing nothing is just as bad as doing the wrong thing' becomes a demand for environmental justice and a non-anthropocentric ethics.

samples.book: 178 - LEGO and Philosophy - Constructing Reality Brick by Brick
samples.title: Notes
samples.relation: Bacharach and Das use Greenpeace's 2014 'Everything is NOT awesome' video — a pristine LEGO Arctic slowly drowning in Shell oil until only a polar bear on a Shell-flagged iceberg remains — to ask what exactly was wrong with LEGO's Shell partnership, and whether a company trading on a wholesome image incurs stricter moral duties. They audit the reality behind the brand: Shell's complicity in Nigeria's repression of the Ogoni and the hanging of Ken Saro-Wiwa, LEGO's outsourcing layoffs in Denmark and the US, and the fact that only about 10 percent of LEGO's carbon emissions come from its own plants, the rest along the supply chain. Their verdict: LEGO is ethically better than most for-profit companies and its fictional Octan satirizes the very consumerism it profits from, but image itself is a fair ground for holding it to a higher standard.

samples.book: 041 - Stephen Colbert and Philosophy - I Am Philosophy (And So Can You!)
samples.title: Who Watches the Watchers
samples.relation: Patton and Webb unpack Colbert's coinage 'freem' — freedom without the do — from the first episode's dedication to 'the heroes' who act patriotically by watching TV, through Bush's post-9/11 call to go shopping, the Wikipedia elephant vandalism, and the WristStrong bracelet as activism indistinguishable from consuming Viacom product. Using Singer's argument that social capital (roads, satellites, infrastructure) makes the 'it's your money' cry hollow, E.O. Wilson's four-Earths arithmetic on unsustainable consumption and greenwashed market 'solutions' to global warming, and Baudrillard's Consumer Society account of news packaged for consumption beside the ads, they ask whether the Colbert Nation's ironic participation resists corporate media or completes it, concluding freem converts even critique into one more purchase.

samples.book: 028 - The Grateful Dead and Philosophy - Getting High Minded about Love and Haight
samples.title: Dizzy with the Possibilities
samples.relation: Allen Thompson treats 'Throwing Stones' — 'the future's here, we are it, we are on our own' — as voicing the existential dread of anthropogenic global warming and the felt 'end of nature' Bill McKibben named, defending the song as the band's a-political polemic against heartless powers. He argues via Steven Vogel that humans cannot literally end nature unless we are supernatural, and recasts the crisis with Thoreau and Gary Snyder as civilization's assault on the wild, the self-willed order we too belong to. Deep ecology then supplies the response: re-identify the self as wild — as Deadheads do by dancing wildly to the music — and build a civilization wildness can endure, with the band's 1988 rainforest-benefit press conference as evidence of the Dead's own ecological consciousness.

samples.book: 131 - Avengers Infinity Saga and Philosophy - Go for the Head
samples.title: 26. Thanos’s Mistake
samples.relation: Argues Thanos embodies Nietzschean master morality — his will as its own justification, 'the hardest choices require the strongest wills,' echoing the Melian dialogue's 'the strong do what they will, the weak suffer what they must,' with Doctor Strange answering in kind ('you'll find our will equal to yours') — while the Avengers speak from slave morality, judging by intentions and branding genocide evil. Thanos's real error, though, is a categorical one: imposing a technical quantity fix (a one-time 50 percent cull) on a social relationship problem, since Hardin's carrying-capacity logic and the St. Matthew Island reindeer show populations must self-limit like apex predators, making his correction a mere stopgap that confuses quantity with relationship.

samples.book: 056 - Dune and Philosophy - Weirding Way of the Mentat
samples.title: The End of the Story
samples.relation: Reads the Gom Jabbar test as Herbert's definition of humanity: Paul endures Mohiam's pain box because a human stays in the trap to turn it on the trapper and protect the species, while an animal only chews off its own leg. The Butlerian Jihad's ban on 'a machine in the likeness of a man's mind' is applied to our own iPod-and-PDA dependence, with Mentat Thufir Hawat showing that losing the machine-crutch 'forced human minds to develop,' in line with Aristotle's phronesis and the politics of the common good (and Plato's contemplation as the core of happiness). The chapter closes by turning the human/animal test on the modern West—Baron Harkonnen-like consumers whose water-hungry beef habit makes us the trap of our own environmental collapse.

samples.book: 192 - Superman and Philosophy - What Would the Man of Steel Do_
samples.title: 15. Infinite Environmental Crisis
samples.relation: A scripted Lois Lane–Batman interview argues that the Batmobile/Batwing upgrade cycle and Wayne Enterprises' multinational production enact Marx's 'metabolic rift' (via John Bellamy Foster): both take from nature and return unprocessable waste faster than the planet can replenish, so protecting Gotham's way of life perpetuates an infinite environmental crisis of consumption. Solar-powered Superman wins the environmental showdown on lifestyle impact, but Batman counters that Krypton's ecological suicide makes Superman an 'environmental refugee,' not a model. The chapter's real verdict is Bruce's line 'We are all Bruce Wayne': human consumers must rebalance the human–nature relationship before finite resources like fresh water run out.

samples.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
samples.title: 29. Frank Herbert’s Dune as Philosophy The Need to Think for Yourself
samples.relation: Reading the Sci Fi Channel miniseries Frank Herbert's Dune and Children of Dune, Littmann argues the saga warns against letting leaders or religions think for us: Paul Atreides fakes being the Fremen Mahdi, wages a holy war, and founds a theocratic tyranny that Alia and Leto II carry to worse extremes. He sets Plato's Republic (the guardian class, the noble lie, rule by the wise) and Hobbes against pro-democracy thinkers—Locke's consent and natural rights, Mill's harm principle, Dewey's democracy—then cites Locke, Paine and Russell on religion's dangers, closing with W.K. Clifford's 'ethics of belief' that one must not accept religious claims without sufficient evidence. The chapter reads Paul's dictatorship and the Bene Gesserit's engineered messiah as dramatizations of the historical abuses of concentrated and religious power.

samples.book: 188 - The Ultimate South Park and Philosophy - Respect My Philosophah!
samples.title: THE ULTIMATE SOUTH PARK AND PHILOSOPHY
samples.relation: Jacoby defends W.K. Clifford's ethics of belief—it is wrong to believe on insufficient evidence and the burden of proof falls on the claimant—through Stan's exposures of TV psychic John Edward ('The Biggest Douche in the Universe'), the Scientology of 'Trapped in the Closet', and the faith-based story of Joseph Smith in 'All About Mormons'. The centerpiece is a South Park-illustrated demolition of Pascal's Wager: Kyle's hemorrhoid-driven despair in 'Cartmanland' shows a perfectly good God would not eternally reward evil Cartman or torture honest nonbelievers, and 'Do the Handicapped Go to Hell?' shows the wagerer cannot even know which religion pays out. Stan's closing speech to Edward's frightened audience carries the moral: comforting lies weaken the mind and slow the progress of finding the real, amazing answers.

samples.book: 146 - The Big Lebowski and Philosophy - Keeping Your Mind Limber with Abiding Wisdom
samples.title: The Big Lebowski and Philosophy
samples.relation: Malloy examines Walter's incorrigible leaps — Bunny kidnapped herself on no evidence, the toe is a fake ('I can get you a toe by three o'clock'), the Big Lebowski can walk — through Clifford's ethics of belief (the ship-owner who sinks his passengers) and James's 'Will to Believe' reply with its living, forced, and momentous genuine options, applied to Walter's 'dabbled' pacifism and his preference for Nazism's ethos over nihilism's nothing. Walter's conversion to Judaism for Cynthia raises whether practice can will belief, tested via Pascal's wager and James's objection, and the verdict borrows Bernard Williams: we cannot choose beliefs, but Walter's reckless policy of dismissing counterevidence makes him 'not just an asshole, he is also wrong'.

samples.book: 134 - KISS and Philosophy - Wiser than Hell
samples.title: 5. Greatness or Nothingness
samples.relation: Courtland Lewis uses KISS's career gambles to compare theories of decision-making. After Tolstoy's twig-over-the-dragon allegory of mortal life, he tests W.K. Clifford's shipowner (never act without sufficient evidence) against KISS's counter-evidence bet on the Alive! live album, models the choice with Pascal's Wager, and uses the Prisoner's Dilemma to explain the flop of the four 1978 solo albums. He then argues William James's pragmatism — beliefs as rules for action, the living, forced, and momentous option that 'KISS is the best' — best explains why acting on the band's self-created narrative was authentic, with Nietzsche completing the picture: greatness requires leaping, living dangerously, tightrope-walking toward self-defined success.

samples.book: 026 - South Park and Philosophy - Bigger, Longer, and More Penetrating
samples.title: Inquiry, Hard Work, and Progress
samples.relation: Jacoby reads Stan Marsh as W.K. Clifford's ethics of belief in action: from 'All About the Mormons' ('you better have something to back it up') to 'The Biggest Douche in the Universe,' Stan insists the burden of proof lies with claimants and that faith used as a fallback is no evidence at all. 'Cartmanland' and the story of Job serve to criticize Pascal's Wager — a good God would not eternally torment the virtuous nonbeliever, and the Wager simply assumes its afterlife payoff — while the harms of Miss Information's holistic healers, David Blaine's cult suicide, and Scientology show Clifford was right that comforting unsupported beliefs weaken minds and, as Stan tells John Edward, slow down the progress of all mankind.

samples.book: 160 - Fallout and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Shelter
samples.title: Notes
samples.relation: Albert Spencer reads Fallout 4's synth crisis as a philosophy-of-mind allegory - Brotherhood dualism, Institute reductive physicalism, Railroad functionalism - which he grounds in the classical pragmatists: Peirce's sign-interpreting mind, James's stream of consciousness, and Dewey's interactive consciousness make personhood a matter of social participation rather than essence. Quests dramatize the stakes: 'Human Error' has Covenant's interrogation of Amelia Stockton enact Du Bois's double consciousness (self-understanding against a devaluing gaze, as with the tragic Phyllis Daily), the Sole Survivor of 'The Battle of Bunker Hill' and Far Harbor becomes Anzaldua's Nepantlera straddling the human/synth binary, and the Railroad's memory-wipe 'resets' reproduce the domination they fight by ignoring Crenshaw's intersectionality (the Feral Historian's case that the Railroad kills the selves it saves). Acadia, where DiMA murdered and replaced Captain Avery to preserve peace, becomes Jane Addams's test case of democracy as associated living - an imperfect, lying community that nonetheless offers the only future of shared synth-human personhood.

samples.book: 196 - Terminator and Philosophy - I'll Be Back, Therefore I Am
samples.title: NOTES
samples.relation: Butler argues the films' humans-versus-machines picture rests on a false dichotomy: we are ourselves 'meat machines,' and functionalism makes minds computational processes realizable in silicon as much as neurons - illustrated by a Henrietta thought experiment (adapted from William Lycan) in which a friend gradually replaced with T-101 parts remains the same conscious person, and refusing this is 'human chauvinism.' Following Dawkins's extended phenotype and Andy Clark's natural-born cyborgs, he claims our tools are components of our minds, so Skynet and even the Terminator films themselves (making Cameron a cyborg of his cameras and editing suites) are extensions of human nature rather than alien 'Others.' Judgment Day, if it came, would be human suicide rather than genocide, so the real question is what values we build into our technology - 'no fate but what we make for ourselves.'

samples.book: 035 - Star Trek and Philosophy - The Wrath of Kant
samples.title: “I Feel Exactly What You Feel”
samples.relation: Runs Star Trek's transporter and android stories as thought experiments on personal identity: the body theory (Kirk rejecting android Korby — 'Dr. Korby was never here' — and Picard telling the resurrected Rishon Uxbridge 'you do not exist'), the brain theory ('Spock's Brain,' Bashir refusing to replace half of Vedek Bareil's brain), and Locke's memory theory as vindicated by the Trill (Lela Dax's 'a person is but the sum of their memories,' the 'Dax' extradition hearing over Curzon's crimes). Riker's transporter double in 'Second Chances' and the Tuvix fusion then break the memory theory through fission and fusion, prompting Parfit's move that psychological continuity, not numerical identity, is what matters in survival. Memory erasure in 'Dagger of the Mind' and Kurn's rebranding after the failed Mauk-to'Vor in 'Sons of Mogh' count as death if we are our memories.

samples.book: 122 - Westworld and Philosophy - Mind Equals Blown
samples.title: “Do you even know where you are ”
samples.relation: Arvan argues the entire series, lab included, literally takes place inside a videogame, citing physically impossible events (Teddy's bullets cannot hurt the Man in Black, William steps onto a moving train, workers appear instantly in a single unbroken shot) and NPC-like loops of the lab staff. He then claims Descartes had it backwards: whether we are in a dream, Spinoza's God's mind, or a simulation (Bostrom's hypothesis, extended by his own peer-to-peer variant that would explain quantum indeterminacy and relativity), to be simulated is still to be real. Via Chalmers-style structuralism, anything structured and functioning like a person is a person, so hosts who walk, talk, love, and suffer are persons — and the humans' rape, torture, and murder of them, like our treatment of Siri and Watson, is dehumanization on a par with slavery and the Holocaust.

samples.book: 068 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Zombie Apocalypse Now
samples.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
samples.relation: Greg Littmann asks whether 'you' survive a walker bite, testing bodily identity, behaviorism, and functionalism as theories of personal survival against Jenner's verdict that after death 'everything you ever were... gone'. His centerpiece adapts Daniel Dennett: survivors yoke walkers to plows and tanks, dangle meat to move them between positions labeled 1 and 0, and gradually build a rope-and-corpse computer functionally identical to a human brain - which behaviorism and functionalism must call conscious, yet which we can conceive as utterly dark inside. The lesson is that we cannot know whether any system, walker, animal, or AI, is conscious, so treatment of non-human systems may need to err on the side of caution.

samples.book: 090 - Dracula and Philosophy - Dying to Know
samples.title: Dracula and Philosophy
samples.relation: McKinney argues Van Helsing should have studied Dracula's brain instead of staking him, because the Count is a philosophy-of-mind thought experiment: a mind that persists unchanged across bat, wolf, mist, and human bodies refutes mind-brain identity theory and fits functionalism (the mind as one song playable in many formats), while his telepathic bond with Mina and shapeshifting probe Cartesian dualism's mind-body interaction problem. Nagel's bats show that only Dracula could tell us what it is like to echo-locate or wolf-sense; yet since nothing like his unconstrained mind exists in our world, the novel finally maps what minds are not - evidence against the immaterial mind.

samples.book: 202 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Shotgun. Machete. Reason
samples.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
samples.relation: Greg Littmann asks whether you survive a walker bite, rejecting the body view via Dr. Jenner's 'Everything you ever were or ever will be—gone' because a mindless corpse is not you. He tests philosophical behaviorism and functionalism against walker behavior—Jenny turning her old doorknob, walkers distinguishing humans by smell—then adapts Dennett's thought experiment into a walker-and-rope computer functionally identical to a human brain. Since we can conceive that groaning machine lacking inner experience, behavior and function cannot settle which systems are conscious, leaving the bitten dying in ignorance of whether they face annihilation or reanimation.

samples.book: 026 - South Park and Philosophy - Bigger, Longer, and More Penetrating
samples.title: The Role of Matter Biology or Function
samples.relation: Lawrence asks which theory of mind best fits the Matrix trilogy. Cartesian dualism (with its pineal-gland plug standing in for Neo's headjack) would explain Neo's jackless mind in the Train Station but lacks evidence and faces the interaction problem, so the chapter defends a fully materialist reading — Neo's sentinel-destroying signal and burnt-eye sight reconstrued as Matrix hardware in his skull. It then contrasts reductive and eliminative materialism, Searle's beer-can biological naturalism, and functionalism via Lewis's Martian pain, concluding that the films' sentient machines — Agent Smith's seamless copy into Bane's body — presuppose functionalism.

samples.book: 030 - Pink Floyd and Philosophy - Careful with that Axiom, Eugene!
samples.title: There is No Dark Side of the Moon Really. Matter of Fact It’s All Dark
samples.relation: Johnston reads The Dark Side of the Moon through Buber's I and Thou: modern life traps us in the I-It mode of experience, from 'Welcome to the Machine' to teachers who treat students as replaceable Its ('Hey, teacher, leave us kids alone!') and Horkheimer's instrumental reason that turns personnel into 'human resources,' while the album repeatedly calls us to the I-You encounter, from 'Echoes'' strangers whose glances meet ('I am you and what I see is me,' Waters's origin of empathy) to 'Breathe''s 'don't be afraid to care.' He links the opening heartbeat and the breath of 'Breathe' to Buber's eternal You, defends Buddhism against Buber's charge that enlightenment is worldless monologue (the Buddha becomes one with the world, a perfect reciprocity like the innate You of the womb), and accepts Nietzsche's point that the Enlightenment's abstract God is dead while insisting, with Buber, that encounter with the eternal You remains possible. The album itself, he concludes, resists degenerating into an It: even if 'the sun is eclipsed by the moon,' the light persists and Dark Side can be the antidote to the It-world.

samples.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
samples.title: Chapter 34 - Beyond Lies the Wub
samples.relation: Dick's first published story dramatizes the moral status of a rational nonhuman: Peterson's wub, a telepathic, philosophical Martian pig-creature, reads minds, discusses Odysseus and individuation, and pleads that it is 'a sensible being like yourselves', yet Captain Franco - obsessed with eating it - freezes it mid-sentence, shoots it looking him in the eye ('Back on the farm we had hogs'), and serves it for dinner, dismissing Peterson's grief with 'It is only organic matter, now.' The wub's personhood is established entirely through language and philosophy, but speech fails to protect it from being treated as meat, and the closing irony - Franco resuming the wub's own Odysseus meditation, as if the mind survived its meal - underscores how thin the line is between person and livestock. The story thus stages the problem of other minds and the ethics of killing sentient beings who demand to be addressed eye-to-eye rather than dined upon.

samples.book: 152 - The Ultimate Daily Show and Philosophy - More Moments of Zen, More Indecision Theory
samples.title: The Ultimate Daily Show and Philosophy
samples.relation: Edelheit, a rabbi, reads Stewart's Jewish persona as an echo of Martin Buber: both disclaim the titles (philosopher, journalist) yet 'point out the window' at what they have seen, and both practice engagement, 'You shall not withhold yourself', with genuine responsibility as real responding, epitomized for him by the face-to-face Crossfire confrontation. He walks through the 'Matzorian Candidate' segment on the Republican Jewish Coalition (the 'Yarmulkometer' ratings, Michele Bachmann's kibbutz years and mispronounced 'chutzpah'), the 'Faith/Off' Passover-versus-Easter segment pitting a chocolate egg against the Seder plate ('Jews! Camera 3'), and Earth (The Book)'s satirically rewritten Binding of Isaac and Reform-Judaism prayer jokes. All of this is read as Buberian dialogue, mocking religion from within rather than at it, and refusing silence in the lineage of Rabbi Joachim Prinz's warning that the most tragic problem is silence.

samples.book: 027 - Hitchcock and Philosophy - Dial M for Metaphysics
samples.title: Bad Faith
samples.relation: Lee reads the 'Breakdown' episode of Alfred Hitchcock Presents existentially: when the executive Callou coldly fires Humka and hangs up on his despair, he treats a person as a thing, Buber's 'I-It' pseudo-listening where Humka sought an 'I-Thou' dialogue with the godlike source of authority in his world. Heidegger's account of inauthenticity explains the mask of rational control behind which Callou hides, and Sartre's bad faith names the self-deception by which he pretends his godlike management of others is justifiable. Paralyzed and taken for a corpse after a car crash, Callou can be saved only when rational strategy fails and he finally weeps: the single tear reveals his caring nature, Jessie addresses him person-to-person, and, vulnerable before God and others, he becomes an authentic self, Hitchcock's pointed moral for bosses who give an employee the sack.

samples.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
samples.title: 79. Cyberpunk 2077 as Philosophy Balancing the (Mystical) Ghost in the (Transhuman) Machine
samples.relation: Lay reads Cyberpunk 2077's transhuman Night City against the enhancement debate. Using the Ship of Theseus, Parfit's continuity plus fission/fusion (V and Johnny 'fusing,' the Delamain AIs) and Clark and Chalmers's extended mind, he argues enhancement neither destroys personal identity (which Parfit says doesn't matter) nor dehumanizes users — it may be the purest expression of Clark's cyborg humanity. The real danger is corporate exploitation of bodies, explained via Adorno's culture industry and Arendt's banality of evil. Buddhist nonattachment (Nagarjuna's emptiness, echoed by a Schopenhauer shard) grounds each ending's pacification-versus-attachment theme, but Lay corrects it with Weil's critique of power and Buber's I-Thou, concluding the game urges transcending the boundary between 'me' and 'you' through mystical interpersonal relation.

samples.book: 181 - Ultimate Lost and Philosophy - Think Together, Die Alone
samples.title: It Worked
samples.relation: Lee reads Jack, Locke, and Desmond as studies in Sartrean bad faith and authenticity: Christian Shephard's Red Sox fatalism is determinism as an excuse for moral failure, Locke swings from a Kierkegaardian leap of faith (pushing the button as his Abraham-and-Isaac trial) into nihilism when the Pearl film suggests the button is a psychological experiment, and Desmond's Humean skepticism yields to sacrificial faith in the fail-safe. He argues Jacob is the show's greatest con man, so Jack's acceptance of destiny in 'The End' remains a free choice rather than predestination. The finale's sideways world then moves Lost from secular existentialism to religious existentialism, read through Buber's I-Thou relation in Sawyer and Juliet's 'It worked' reunion and the all-religions church, where as Gandhi held every path leads to the same place.

samples.book: 288 - Dating – Philosophy for Everyone - Flirting With Big Ideas
samples.title: DATING PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE
samples.relation: Silber uses his own Match.com romance with Karin to argue that virtual 'meeting' differs phenomenologically from face-to-face meeting, which Buber's I-Thou (vs I-It) makes into a whole-being encounter that online traces and aspects cannot supply, invoking 'all real living is meeting.' He treats the dating market as a site of Kantian danger, contrasting price with the dignity of persons in the kingdom of ends, and warns that the market's efficiency threatens objectification and commodification. He then deploys Sartre's bad faith, facticity and transcendence, and 'existence precedes essence' to diagnose online self-misrepresentation (lying about height, age, photos) as inauthenticity, while briefly setting Derrida's 'nothing outside the text' against Plato's Phaedrus preference for speech over writing.

samples.book: 241 - The Philosophy of Documentary Film
samples.title: 26_LaRocca_Chapter_025.html
samples.relation: Bill Nichols writes an open letter to Errol Morris explaining his bodily 'revulsion' at Standard Operating Procedure, Morris's film on the Abu Ghraib torture photographs. Nichols gives three reasons: the painfully limited, remorseless perspective of the MP guards elevated to mythic screen scale; the morally impossible reenactment tracking shots that put the viewer in the torturers' point of view (compared to Schindler's List); and the total absence of the Iraqi detainees' voices. He faults Morris for decontextualizing and fetishizing the images and forfeiting a moral center, contrasting the film with Rithy Panh's S-21, and casts the missing ethical encounter in terms of Buber's I-Thou relation of mutual honesty while wishing he had Fanon's capacity to treat the perpetrators' suffering.

samples.book: 152 - The Ultimate Daily Show and Philosophy - More Moments of Zen, More Indecision Theory
samples.title: The Ultimate Daily Show and Philosophy
samples.relation: Dempsey catalogs how The Daily Show and The Colbert Report expose political rhetoric by ridicule: ad hominem attacks on Judge Anna Diggs Taylor's wiretapping ruling, the straw man 'cut and run' distortion of John Murtha, Zell Miller's RNC outrage, false dilemmas ('with us or with the terrorists', Colbert's 'great president or the greatest president?'), slippery slopes from same-sex marriage to snake marriage, Tony Snow's equivocation on 'fit for duty', and Sam Brownback's question-begging snowflake-baby presentation against stem-cell research. He then treats emotional appeals (the 9/11-saturated 2004 RNC, Kerry's 'reporting for duty', Colbert's fear-mongering 'ThreatDown' and flag-wrapped patriotism) and spin as the systematic use of persuasive language: euphemism and dysphemism ('socialist', 'war on ______'), rhetorical definition of abortion as 'murder', 'Polish that Turd' jobs-number spinning, the GOP memo read aloud on Fox News, and Bush's Iraq-versus-North Korea double standard. Montages lay the talking-point machinery bare, and the chapter argues a critically informed citizenry is the democratic defense against elites who distrust the public with the truth.

samples.book: 075 - Psych and Philosophy - Some Dark Juju-Magumbo
samples.title: Psych and Philosophy
samples.relation: Michaud argues that Shawn's whole psychic career runs on fallacies of relevance - the red herring of claiming to be psychic to dodge arrest, plus ad hominem mockery that deflects Lassiter's fraud accusations - so the show's comedy turns on bad logic being used to lead people to true conclusions. Socrates supplies the opposing voice: like the Sophists who argued any side for money, Shawn reasons for convenience and amusement, and his deception is an inconsistency of the kind Socrates refused in Plato's Crito, where he would not bribe his way out of a death sentence. An invented Platonic-style dialogue has Socrates question Shawn until he concedes that lying breeds more lying and harm - 'her name is Truth!' - before Shawn escapes the elenchus by spotting lipstick on Socrates's collar. The chapter leaves the verdict open: Shawn saves lives and raises the world's happiness, but his trickery also trains Santa Barbara to reason badly and trust con artists.

samples.book: 188 - The Ultimate South Park and Philosophy - Respect My Philosophah!
samples.title: THE ULTIMATE SOUTH PARK AND PHILOSOPHY
samples.relation: Arp uses the show as a logic textbook: his own prejudice against Goth kids and Officer Barbrady's post-Atlas Shrugged ban on books illustrate hasty generalization, Cartman's 'if you do drugs, then you're a hippie' chain and the Tooth Fairy syllogism illustrate deductive argument, and Towelie's appearances illustrate inductive strength. A fallacy catalog follows: Johnny Cochran's 'If Chewbacca lives on Endor, you must acquit' in 'Chef Aid' as red herring, Mrs. Broflovski's 'Death' boycott of Terrance and Phillip as slippery slope, Mrs. Marsh's cookie outburst in 'Clubhouses' as hasty generalization plus slippery slope, Father Maxi's hell pronouncements as appeal to inappropriate authority, and cartoon Rob Reiner in 'Butt Out' as ad hominem. The chapter's claim is that Parker and Stone deliberately violate logical principles episode after episode to expose absurd beliefs, because how people reason shapes the laws they make and the beliefs they die for.

samples.book: 091 - It's Always Sunny and Philosophy - The Gang Gets Analyzed
samples.title: It’s Always Sunny and Philosophy
samples.relation: Fenner Tanswell uses 'Reynolds vs. Reynolds: The Cereal Defense' - the Gang's in-bar trial over Frank's blind driving versus Dennis's cereal-at-the-wheel - as a catalogue of crooked thinking. We get valid forms distinguished from soundness (modus ponens with 'if poop is funny, then Frank pooped in the bed'; Charlie's modus tollens from Frank's no-donkey-brains certificate), then the fallacies: the argument from ignorance by which Dennis's lacking a certificate proves him donkey-brained, Dee's ad hominem against Mac, Dennis's appeal to authority, and Mac's 'Science Is a Liar Sometimes' poster, which equivocates between mere skeptical doubt (even Descartes's) and reasonable doubt by straw-manning science as claiming infallibility. True to form, the Gang convicts Dee 'for comedy rather than on any logical basis.'

samples.book: 116 - 1984 and Philosophy - Is Resistance Futile
samples.title: 5. Ministry of Truth Handbook Excerpt on the Strategic Use of Fallacious Reasoning for Thoughtcrime Prevention
samples.relation: Rard's satirical Party handbook explains how to keep a population from thinking: keep the proles too poor and exhausted to reason, and deploy fallacies strategically, from ad hominem goat-caricatures of Goldstein at the Two Minutes Hate and straw man versions of his arguments, to destroying contrary evidence, appealing to fear of the old capitalist world, and Room 101's appeal to force, so false beliefs can be manufactured as easily as true ones. It presents Plato's noble lie as the Ministry's founding inspiration, calling the reader's mission 'a continuation of Plato's dream'. It also cites Aristotle's view that emotion must be disciplined for reason to work, which the Party inverts by deliberately triggering fear and hatred to disable rational thought.

samples.book: 179 - The Legend of Zelda and Philosophy - Link Outside the Box
samples.title: End Game
samples.relation: Robert Arp and Dennis Milarker teach informal logic through Zelda, opening with Arp's own fallacious 'all gamers are geeks' hasty generalization and stereotypes about Miyamoto's Japanese heritage. They standard-form arguments about which Zelda game is chronologically first, distinguish deductive from inductive reasoning (the Best Buy Wii camp-out, expectations for The Adventure of Link's side-scrolling perspective), and run through fallacies: inappropriate authority, the Atari false dilemma (the TV was on channel 4), equivocation on release order versus story order, ad hominem, and the slippery slope against Doom and Grand Theft Auto. The lesson is that Ganon and gamers alike must give good arguments, since bad reasoning shapes laws, beliefs, and lives.

samples.book: 036 - The Legend of Zelda and Philosophy - I Link Therefore I Am
samples.title: End Game
samples.relation: Arp and Milarker use Zelda examples to teach informal logic: Rob's 'all gamers are geeks' is a hasty generalization, the argument that the original Zelda is chronologically first commits equivocation (Earth release order is not Hyrule chronology, since Miyamoto named Ocarina of Time earliest), and debates over banning violent games trade in false dilemmas, ad hominem, and slippery slopes. The chapter sets out premises, conclusions, deductive versus inductive arguments, validity and soundness, strength and cogency, with worked examples from Clawshot reasoning to Best Buy Wii lines. Its point is that fallacious reasoning harms real lives, so readers should audit every argument in the book and in the gaming world.

samples.book: 026 - South Park and Philosophy - Bigger, Longer, and More Penetrating
samples.title: The Defense Rests
samples.relation: Arp uses 'Chef Aid' — cartoon Johnnie Cochran's 'If Chewbacca lives on Endor, you must acquit' — to introduce the red herring fallacy, then teaches the basics of logic through South Park: Cartman's Tooth Fairy argument as deduction, Towelie's appearances as induction, and episodes like 'The Entity,' 'Weight Gain 4000,' and 'Butt Out' illustrating hasty generalization, slippery slope, false dilemma, appeal to inappropriate authority, and ad hominem. His point is that Parker and Stone deliberately violate logical principles for humor, and that spotting fallacies matters because bad reasoning drives laws, policies, and the beliefs people die for.

samples.book: 104 - Red Rising and Philosophy - Break the Chains!
samples.title: 13. Mustang’s Future Generations
samples.relation: Courtland Lewis asks what Mustang owes future generations when rebuilding the Society, first showing that standard moral theories stall: nonexistent people lack rationality, cannot contract, cannot be treated virtuously, and utilitarian forecasting fails since we cannot know whether the Jackal's nuking of Luna might have led, in the deep future, to prosperity. Derek Parfit's Reasons and Persons then strikes: any policy choice creates a different future generation, total utility drives the Repugnant Conclusion (a maximally populous world of barely-worth-living lives, uncomfortably like the Society's Reds), and average utility yields the mere addition paradox (Mustang's Society is both no worse off and worse off when Andromeda's low-pleasure civilization is added). The chapter's solution is Rawls: the original position behind the veil of ignorance—where the Sovereign would not know she is a Gold—yields justice as fairness and maximin reasoning for the just savings problem, choosing to save more than is consumed; against Tim Mulgan's objection that this loops back to the Repugnant Conclusion, Lewis answers that real carrying capacities make the repugnant world impossible.

samples.book: 038 - Radiohead and Philosophy - Fitter Happier More Deductive
samples.title: Go Slowly
samples.relation: Wittkower frames In Rainbows' pay-what-you-want release with Adorno and Horkheimer's culture industry: music is expressive communication awkwardly trapped in commodity form — even 'Happy Birthday' has an owner until 2030 — and digital distribution is finally tearing that frame down. He then applies Rawls's justice as fairness to music distribution: the first principle now supports everyone's liberty to listen, rip, and share, because viable alternative models mean restricting listeners can no longer be justified as necessary to artists; and the difference principle, with the sadists-objection to utilitarian aggregation, shows that how benefits are distributed among persons matters, which he extends to racial wealth gaps and the affirmative-action dilemma. His conclusion is that we must 'go slowly': listeners' rights to their culture outweigh labels' legitimate profit expectations, the way emancipation outweighed plantation business models, and labels must adapt into service providers rather than gatekeepers.

samples.book: 072 - Jeopardy! and Philosophy - What Is Knowledge in the Form of a Question
samples.title: Jeopardy! and Philosophy
samples.relation: Shaun Young tests Jeopardy! against equality as an 'essentially contested concept': Aristotle's proportional equality (treat like cases as like) seems to justify the winner-take-all payout as deserved, Locke's reward for the industrious explains why equal outcomes would kill incentive, and Rawls's two principles - fair equality of opportunity plus the difference principle - capture the show's identical rules and level playing field. He then raises harder challenges: Dworkin's equality of resources, Kymlicka's charge that the Americo-centric clue bank shortchanges minority cultures (with Quebec's Bill 101 as legitimate differentiated rights), and the capabilities approach of Sen and Nussbaum applied to would-be contestants who cannot operate the signaling device. Citing Isaiah Berlin's pluralism, he concludes that no final verdict on Jeopardy!'s equality is possible - and that spectators would not want one, since Jennings's seventy-four-game streak thrills precisely because of inequality between players.

samples.book: 171 - House of Cards and Philosophy - Underwood's Republic
samples.title: Notes
samples.relation: Kogelmann argues that political philosophers' ideal theory rests on Rawls's 'strict compliance' assumption — the West Wing picture where citizens and politicians pursue the public good — while House of Cards depicts the reality: Russo's zoning constituent, the teachers' union fighting performance standards, Senator Haas and Sharp's colleagues trading votes for self-interest. By the theory of the second best, ideals designed for selfless politicians misfire in a world with Frank and Remy Danton in it, so he recruits the older 'every man a knave' tradition — Adam Smith's self-love turned to public benefit, Hume's maxim, Madison's ambition-countering-ambition, Buchanan's 'politics without romance' — to redesign institutions against rent-seeking (SanCorp's purchase of votes on Russo's watershed bill) and politicians' short election-cycle horizons (Claire courting Senator Mendoza), via public financing and balanced-budget and inflation rules.

samples.book: 133 - Perry Mason and Philosophy - The Case of the Awesome Attorney
samples.title: 2. A Paragon of Righteous Virtue
samples.relation: Allinson reads Gardner's novels, especially The Case of the Blonde Bonanza, as philosophy disguised as pulp: Mason acts from curiosity, compassion, and justice rather than utility, a 'pure Kantian or ancient Confucian' deontologist whose loyalty to clients ('erase ATTORNEY AT LAW from the door') functions as his own Categorical Imperative. The chapter's crux is the perjury dilemma of the Blonde Bonanza: Mrs. Winlock's offered false testimony would free Dianne Alder, which Mason twice refuses yet curses ('To hell with it'), showing that the plot's deus ex machina dissolves but never solves the ethical dilemma, while George Winlock's truth-telling-at-any-cost mirrors Kant's prohibition on lying even to the Gestapo. Socrates's better-to-suffer-evil, Plato's Meno reversal, Aristotle's rhetoric, Confucian and Hebrew filial piety in Dianne's character, and Rawls's justice as fairness all serve as lenses on Mason's virtues.

samples.book: 170 - House and Philosophy - Everybody Lies
samples.title: Notes
samples.relation: Argues that Rawls' ideal theory rests on a 'strict compliance' assumption — citizens and politicians who pursue justice rather than self-interest — which makes his ideal society look like The West Wing, while House of Cards depicts the real one: teachers' unions fighting performance standards, Senator Haas blocking the omnibus bill for electoral fear, Jackie Sharp trading favors, and SanCorp's Remy Danton buying votes against Russo's watershed bill. The chapter traces the competing 'every man a knave' tradition — Smith's invisible hand converting the butcher's self-love into our dinner, Hume's maxim for constitution-designers, Madison's 'ambition counteract ambition', and Buchanan's public choice revival — and uses the theory of the second best to argue we must design institutions (publicly financed elections, balanced-budget and inflation amendments, a generality constraint) that assume Underwoods run for Congress.

samples.book: 098 - The Princess Bride and Philosophy - Inconceivable!
samples.title: 3. The Magic of a Promise
samples.relation: Alloy reads the whole story as being about promises - Westley's 'I will always come for you,' Humperdinck's insincerely made and casually broken vows to Buttercup, and Inigo's vow of vengeance to his murdered father. He tests conventionalism, using Rawls's idea that breaking a promise cheats on a fair rule-bound practice (illustrated by Inigo's rule-governed duel and the Battle of Wits where both parties cheat), against expectationalism, on which obligation comes from the trust and expectations created, as when Humperdinck manipulates Buttercup through her trust. Both theories struggle with Inigo's promise to a dead man, so Alloy argues with Searle that it is responsibility for intent that makes a promise, and defends his own view - against the Hobbesian consensus - that every promise is also a self-promise whose binding force is the promisor's self-respect: promises 'make us people.'

samples.book: 149 - Black Panther and Philosophy - What Can Wakanda Offer the World_
samples.title: 3 Sins of the Fathers Historical Injustice and Its Repair in lack Panther
samples.relation: Almassi contrasts Rawlsian ideal theory (the veil of ignorance, justice as fairness) with Charles Mills's critique that idealization marginalizes actual historic oppression, arguing the film's characters seek Aristotle's corrective justice in a world already steeped in wrongdoing: the 1991 deaths of W'Kabi's parents at Klaue's hands and of N'Jobu at T'Chaka's. He works through the Museum of Great Britain axe scene as restitution, W'Kabi's 'you kill him where he stands' and Killmonger's 'I'mma make sure we're even' as retribution (tested against Walen's proportionality principles, with vengeance untethered from legitimate punishment), and Nakia's and T'Challa's outreach centers as Margaret Urban Walker-style relational repair, reading T'Chaka's concealment of N'Jobu's death as actively constructed ignorance in service of isolationism.

samples.book: 112 - The Americans and Philosophy - Reds in the Bed
samples.title: 4 On the Origin of the State
samples.relation: Opening with Newt Gingrich's complaint that students 'don't read enough Locke' and the Chinese premier's appeal to Rousseau, the chapter compares the three contract theorists' states of nature and purposes of government: Hobbes's war of every man against every man yielding an absolute sovereign with no separation of powers, Locke's peaceful nature in which mixing labor with land creates property and money then creates inequality, so that government's 'great and chief end' is protecting property through limited, separated powers and no food stamps, and Rousseau's compassionate natural humans corrupted when the first man enclosed land, so the state was founded on fraud and a general will that should 'force him to be free' and give people food stamps. Smith then reads the actual US founding as a chaste Lockean contract 'bastardized' on race and sex - the Declaration plagiarized from Locke, Abigail Adams's 'remember the ladies' laughed off, Dred Scott, with the 14th Amendment as the de-bastardizing 'Charter of Universal Freedom' - while Engels derives the state historically from the Iroquois and Greek gens, private property and class conflict.
