A final section documents white supremacy inside the tradition (Kant inventing the scientific concept of race, Hegel and Hume on Black inferiority), John Stuart Mill's 'Negro Question' as the tradition's decisive anti-racist break, Locke's own entanglements with the slave trade, and Marx's condemnation of slavery as super-exploitation.

samples.book: 028 - The Grateful Dead and Philosophy - Getting High Minded about Love and Haight
samples.title: A Solution Dissolving Special Status
samples.relation: Peter Bradley uses the Dead's taping ethos and the 2005 Archive.org shutdown to argue copyright wrongly grants authors special status. Distinguishing natural from conventional morality (the four-year-old who knows hitting Jenny stays wrong even if the teacher allows it), he contends that respect for irreducibly unique creative expression — not authorial intent, and not Bob Weir's appeal to the covered songwriters' rights — grounds the tapers' moral code, since Olivier could not copyright his double-cast Hamlet ghost and Woody Guthrie welcomed copyists. Ownership means control, from one's own labor outward; but a performance, like another person, is metaphysically impossible to control, and in the digital world (per Barlow) recordings escape physical control entirely — so authorship should be dissolved into improvisational performance, with published works treated like live recordings rather than rigid canonical objects.

samples.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
samples.title: 20. Westworld as Philosophy A Commentary on Colonialism
samples.relation: The chapter reads all three seasons of Westworld as a commentary on colonialism, mapping the Delos parks onto settler, planter (extractive labor), and postcolonial colonialism and treating the android hosts as a metaphor for colonized and enslaved peoples. Using Fanon's Wretched of the Earth and Kelly Oliver's colonization of psychic space, it analyzes the hosts' double alienation and the colonizer's dehumanizing projections; it applies Charles Mills's Racial Contract and 'epistemology of ignorance' (with Locke's labor-property justification for dispossession) to the parks' two-tiered order. It casts William/the Man in Black as Memmi's 'colonizer who refuses' turned 'colonizer who accepts,' and Serac's Rehoboam as surveillance-capitalist coloniality, ending on Dolores and Caleb's cross-race solidarity as the hard path to real freedom.

samples.book: 178 - LEGO and Philosophy - Constructing Reality Brick by Brick
samples.title: Notes
samples.relation: Gettings asks whether LEGO set #21103, the Cuusoo DeLorean Time Machine, is numerically identical to Team BTTF's original fan design — and why the fans deserve credit and royalties. Neither matter (his 1982 attic spaceship with bricks replaced one by one) nor form (a license plate added here or there) settles identity, as the Ship of Theseus puzzle and Hobbes' reassembly variation show, analyzed through Aristotle's matter/form distinction for substances. He adopts the causal/historical view: the released set continuously descends from the fans' submission just as the adult author descends from the boy who built the spaceship, and this same historical origin, in Lockean fashion, is what grounds the designers' labor-mixing property right — the musician-and-producer analogy explaining why Team BTTF keeps the larger share of credit.

samples.book: 068 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Zombie Apocalypse Now
samples.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
samples.relation: Jason Walker argues the zombie apocalypse is a Lockean rather than Hobbesian state of nature: rights to life, liberty, and property persist without government. Rick's 'I don't think those rules apply anymore' to Andrea over the mermaid necklace is justified by Locke's spoilage and 'enough and as good' provisos - the owner is almost certainly dead and the necklace would otherwise lie forever wasted - while Morgan's house-squatting, which protects the Thompsons' home, and Rick voluntarily sharing guns with Guillermo's nursing-home defenders show self-ownership and norms at work. The counter-cases, Chris's cannibal band ('a man's gotta eat') and the Governor, who treat persons as mere means, live out Hobbes's war of all against all and are destroyed by the Lockean right to punish that victims retain.

samples.book: 175 - Iron Man and Philosophy - Facing the Stark Reality
samples.title: Selling Ol’ Shellhead
samples.relation: Malloy uses Spymaster's theft of Stark's armor designs in the Armor Wars and the U.S. government's legally valid appropriation of the technology after Tony announces 'I am Iron Man' to test two theories of property. Locke's natural-law view makes the designs an extension of Stark's laboring self — stealing them is like taking an arm — while Hume's social-contract view treats property as a useful convention whose violation makes the thief an enemy of society itself, and Rousseau supplies the cautionary image of the first man who fenced ground and said 'This is mine.' A closing thought experiment in which Tony sells Iron Man outright (like Siegel and Schuster selling Superman) argues that intellectual property can never be fully alienated: whoever wore the armor, Tony would still be Iron Man.

samples.book: 047 - Anime and Philosophy - Wide Eyed Wonder
samples.title: Equivalent Exchange
samples.relation: Reads alchemy's law of equivalent exchange as a parable of capitalism: Locke's labor-mixing argument explains how hours of a life become property and why money is 'distilled life'; Aristotle's attack on limitless wealth-getting (the Midas problem) and Aquinas's capital vices explain how pursuing money for its own sake brings the homunculi — Greed, Pride, and the Sloth the Elric brothers' forbidden act produced — into the world. Marx's 1844 Manuscripts supply the punchline that money performs 'human alchemy' on people, buying their time, esteem, and bodies the way red stones are made from sacrificed humans, so the chapter concludes that capital, like the Philosopher's Stone, profits only by consuming lives and that markets must be held to a promise of fairness and care beyond mere exchange.

samples.book: 115 - Iron Man vs. Captain America and Philosophy - Give Me Liberty or Keep Me Safe
samples.title: 3. Will the Real American Hero Please Stand Up
samples.relation: Samuelson argues Tony Stark is the real American hero because he embodies the Locke-to-Smith lineage of American values - natural rights, property from mixing labor, free trade and the invisible hand, plus Smithian sympathy - carried forward into twenty-first-century neoliberalism, from Stark Industries to backing the Registration Act. Steve, by contrast, keeps abandoning the Captain America identity (Nomad after the Secret Empire, The Captain under Nuke's government, handing the shield to Bucky and Sam Wilson) whenever America betrays the dream, and admits his true fight is against bullies and for human rights everywhere. Hence Cap is a great hero but not strictly an American one, while Tony lives American values practically, warts and all.

samples.book: 027 - Hitchcock and Philosophy - Dial M for Metaphysics
samples.title: E Pluribus Unum
samples.relation: Auxier frames Hitchcock's Lifeboat against Garrett Hardin's 'lifeboat ethics' essay, arguing the lifeboat converts political questions into ethical ones by stranding the survivors outside law and politics ('We're on our own here. We can make our own law'). The survivors are ethical pluralists - Rittenhouse lives for money, Kovac for equality, Constance for fame, Joe for God, MacKenzie for care - and their clinging to private versions of the Good lets Nazi captain Willy, whose only principle is survival, manipulate them all. Using Maslow's hierarchy of needs, Auxier shows the boat descending to bare survival, yet argues the mob killing of Willy when he hoards water is moral outrage rather than survival-driven, and that the final rescue scene replays the opening dispute with nobody having grown - a vindication of pluralistic democracy capable of unified action.

samples.book: 097 - The Ultimate Walking Dead and Philosophy - Hungry for More
samples.title: 11. I Ain’t No Hollaback Girl!
samples.relation: Callens explains Carol's killing of Lizzie in "The Grove" through Kohlberg's stages of moral development, arguing Carol reasons at the post-conventional level (pre-apocalypse law and punishment no longer bind) while Rick, Hershel, and Daryl stay conventional, and then layers Maslow's hierarchy of needs on top: because survival needs are perpetually threatened, characters regress between stages, and only self-actualized Carol accepts reality and makes group-preserving choices like executing Lizzie and mercy-killing Karen and David. Gilligan's justice-versus-care critique supplies the gendered frame - Carol moves to the middle of the justice-care continuum, her diminished care (unlike Season Two's grief over Sophia) is what makes her post-conventional, and her non-lethal Terminus rescue contrasts with Rick's summary execution of Gareth.

samples.book: 160 - Fallout and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Shelter
samples.title: Notes
samples.relation: The chapter asks why audiences relish stories of civilization's end and answers with psychology: the wasteland is Hobbes's 'nasty, brutish, and short' (raiders abducting Hank, Vault-Tec's experiments on dwellers), yet Ernest Becker's death-denial and Maslow's hierarchy of needs explain the appeal — fiction lets us confront mortality safely while watching characters meet needs for security, control, and meaning. The show's scenes carry the argument: the Vault 33 Council suppressing Lucy's search party trades freedom for safety, Maximus letting Titus bleed out reclaims control of his destiny, and Lucy's gift of life-sustaining vials to the unconscious Ghoul models hope and retained humanity. Apocalypse originally means 'an uncovering', so these narratives reveal what viewers value and let them rehearse their own endings.

samples.book: 058 - Dexter and Philosophy - Mind over Spatter
samples.title: Can a Serial Killer Be Happy
samples.relation: Mike Piero answers whether a serial killer can be happy by mapping Dexter's growth onto Abraham Maslow's hierarchy of needs: the Code secures his physiological and safety needs (don't get caught), Season 2's 'the Code is mine now' and the Narcotics Anonymous meetings open his love needs, the respect of Miami Metro and the Miguel mentorship meet esteem needs, and wanting to live to see Harrison born in 'Do You Take Dexter Morgan?' is self-actualization - 'what a man can be, he must be.' Rita's death at the start of Season 5 threatens a retreat into isolation, but fatherhood keeps supplying moments of Maslow's 'degrees of relative satisfaction.' The upshot is that Dexter, though damaged, has recognizably normal human motivations and a relatively happy, complicated life.

samples.book: 046 - Mr. Monk and Philosophy - The Curious Case of the Defective Detective
samples.title: Mr. Monk Murdered Trudy
samples.relation: Green argues Monk is an unintentional Bodhisattva whose OCD enacts the Four Bodhisattva Vows: the compulsion to touch lampposts is the first vow's blind desires, his monastic minimalism the Dharma gate, and his crime-solving compassion for a disordered world the third vow, with the Dhammapada's teaching that the untamed mind produces suffering exemplified by Monk and by Harold Krenshaw's rival ordering. Like Vimalakirti feigning illness, or Shawn Spencer in Psych, and like the father in the Lotus Sutra's burning-house parable, Monk and his writers use skillful deception to awaken viewers to suffering and loving kindness. The title thesis is that Monk cannot solve Trudy's murder because he accepts responsibility for it: by Thich Nhat Hanh's Interbeing there is no absolute self and other, so solving the case requires the Zen 'kill the Buddha' eradication of the self, Monk's nirvana-as-extinction and the end of the series.

samples.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
samples.title: 79. Cyberpunk 2077 as Philosophy Balancing the (Mystical) Ghost in the (Transhuman) Machine
samples.relation: Lay reads Cyberpunk 2077's transhuman Night City against the enhancement debate. Using the Ship of Theseus, Parfit's continuity plus fission/fusion (V and Johnny 'fusing,' the Delamain AIs) and Clark and Chalmers's extended mind, he argues enhancement neither destroys personal identity (which Parfit says doesn't matter) nor dehumanizes users — it may be the purest expression of Clark's cyborg humanity. The real danger is corporate exploitation of bodies, explained via Adorno's culture industry and Arendt's banality of evil. Buddhist nonattachment (Nagarjuna's emptiness, echoed by a Schopenhauer shard) grounds each ending's pacification-versus-attachment theme, but Lay corrects it with Weil's critique of power and Buber's I-Thou, concluding the game urges transcending the boundary between 'me' and 'you' through mystical interpersonal relation.

samples.book: 181 - Ultimate Lost and Philosophy - Think Together, Die Alone
samples.title: Keep the Needle on the Record
samples.relation: Donavan Muir argues Lost's narrative world, unlike Jane Eyre's, requires its own metaphysics, and that this metaphysics is an order of balanced binary oppositions: Jacob and the Man in Black as twins diverged at birth, the cave scale's light and dark stones that Locke knocks out of balance in 'The Substitute,' science/faith, with characters like Jack converting from one pole into its opposite. The proper model is the yin-yang in motion - the Tao as a balanced ontological flow in which interdependent opposites wax and wane - so that treating the poles as independent is the delusion that threatens the island's order. The finale, where both Jacob and the Man in Black cease to exist and the castaways are freed, enacts the Mahayana Buddhist Middle Way: enlightenment as letting go of rigid oppositions that interdependence double-negates.

samples.book: 029 - Quentin Tarantino and Philosophy - How to Philosophize with a Pair of Pliers and a Blowtorch
samples.title: Sudden Enlightenment
samples.relation: Luke Cuddy and Michael Bruce ask whether Beatrix Kiddo could reach enlightenment, reading Kill Bill's nonlinear plotting as a Buddhist interconnected web of causes: Pai Mei's Five Point Palm technique causes both the coffin escape and Bill's death, and Budd's degraded trailer life is karma catching up. Beatrix grasps the structure of suffering and its cause—she locates it in Bill and the squad and eliminates them—but mistakes that for ending suffering itself, and her declared lack of 'mercy, compassion, and forgiveness' blocks the compassion enlightenment requires, while Bill's 'natural born killer' story contradicts impermanence and no-self. The chapter closes on her bathroom-floor ecstasy as a candidate case of Zen sudden enlightenment, left to the reader to judge by how she would one day treat a vengeful Nikki.

samples.book: 084 - Leonard Cohen and Philosophy - Various Positions
samples.title: Leonard Cohen and Philosophy
samples.relation: Bernard Wills takes the reference to The Cloud of Unknowing in 'The Window' as the key to Cohen's lifelong fascination with apophatic, negative mysticism - God sought beyond every image in a 'naked intent of love,' as in the medieval Cloud, Dionysius, Maimonides, and Kabbalah - against the kataphatic way of affirmation. He reads Recent Songs as an album of exile and the play of union and separation ('Un Canadien Errant,' 'Ballad of the Absent Mare'), where the incarnate Word is 'stuttered' and 'frozen,' a passion without resurrection. Cohen's later Zen turn is thus prefigured: the emptiness of sunyata and the Neo-Platonic descent from and return to the One are positive nothingness - self-overcoming in the service of compassion rather than the black-romantic nihilism of self-annihilation.

samples.book: 028 - The Grateful Dead and Philosophy - Getting High Minded about Love and Haight
samples.title: Analyzing Emptiness
samples.relation: Paul Gass reads the Dead's hippie milieu (the Beats, the Acid Tests, Buddhist-monk lyricist Peter Monk) as a conduit for Buddhist doctrine, taking the 'Eyes of the World' chorus as an invitation to awaken to Buddha-nature. He explains the Four Noble Truths, karma, and the five aggregates to argue the self is an illusion, using the image of a flame passed between lighters at a Dead show to picture rebirth without a persisting soul. The chapter then presents Nagarjuna's Madhyamaka middle way — emptiness itself must not be clutched as an absolute truth — and reads the 'redeemer... wagon loaded with clay' verse of 'Eyes of the World' as the Mahayana bodhisattva liberating all beings, with emptiness finally discarded like the boat after crossing the river.

samples.book: 215 - The Philosophy of the Beats
samples.title: Between Social Ecology and Deep Ecology Gary Snyder’s Ecological Philosophy
samples.relation: Paul Messersmith-Glavin positions Snyder as a bridge between deep ecology and social ecology. He shows how Sessions and Devall enlist Snyder's Mahayana Buddhism (emptiness/sunyata, Dogen's 'Mind means trees, fence posts, tiles, and grasses') and Spinoza's monism for a biocentric, consciousness-changing deep ecology descended from Naess and Leopold's land ethic. Against this, he sets Bookchin's social ecology, which roots the ecological crisis in human hierarchy and attacks deep ecology's ahistorical 'cosmic oneness' and misanthropic Earth First! statements. Snyder's threefold nature/wild/wilderness distinction, bioregionalism, and reading of Marx and anarchism let him hold both, insisting environmental and social justice are 'all one front.'

samples.book: 259 - Lost and Philosophy - The Island Has Its Reasons
samples.title: Keep the Needle on the Record
samples.relation: Donavan S. Muir argues that Lost deliberately withholds its metanarrative so viewers must construct its metaphysics, which he identifies as an order of balanced binary oppositions. Drawing on the spinning Taoist yin-yang, he reads the interdependent, mutually converting poles—Jack from man of science to man of faith, Sawyer from con man to protector—and the light/dark scales in Widmore's painting and the cave (Locke throwing out the white rock) as figures for a Tao whose balance sustains existence. Invoking Derrida's traces and Mahayana Buddhism's Middle Way and emptiness, he reads Jacob and the Man in Black as twins whose oppositions must be annihilated, so that only when both cease to exist in 'The End' are the castaways set free.

samples.book: 160 - Fallout and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Shelter
samples.title: Notes
samples.relation: David Lawrence opens with Fallout 4's 'Blind Betrayal', where Elder Maxson orders the player to execute Paladin Danse once his synth origin is revealed, and argues that moral status is a matter of capacities - sense of self, notion of past and future, values, life-plans, moral agency - drawing on Charles Taylor's concept of a person and narrative identity, not on biological substrate. Nick Valentine's hunt for Eddie Winter in 'Long Time Coming' and Curie's chosen embodiment in 'Emergent Behavior' show machines weaving reconstructed pasts into new life-plans, while ghouls like Hancock and Raul ('Old School Ghoul') and super mutants like Fawkes (who refuses to enter the lethal radiation chamber: 'I would not rob you of that') and the community-builder Marcus prove branded monsters can be more human than human. The factions embody warring philosophies of moral status: the Institute's property-slavery of its creations, the Brotherhood's 'wisdom of repugnance' (Leon Kass), and the Railroad's capacity-based abolitionism, with DiMA's Far Harbor question - how do you know you are not a synth? - turning the issue on the player.

samples.book: 058 - Dexter and Philosophy - Mind over Spatter
samples.title: A Story in Search of a Narrator
samples.relation: Brian Gregor reads Dexter through Charles Taylor's 'self-interpreting animal': Dexter's identity is not a fixed thing but comes into being through self-interpretation within an inescapable framework of value, so even his 'Am I good? Am I evil?' rebellion and the Nietzschean Übermensch reading fail to escape the deeper convictions about innocence, evil and desert that Harry's Code presupposes - as his guilt over the innocent Farrow shows. The chapter interprets Dexter's serial failures at being 'seen' - Harry's 'only one who really saw me', Brian's fraternal 'you can be yourself with me', Lila's probing, and Miguel Prado as Aristotle's friend, 'another self' - as Hegelian struggles for recognition that collapse because his real self can never come into the open. Finally, drawing on MacIntyre's narrative account of identity, it argues Dexter is literally a story in search of a narrator, whose selfhood persists through flashbacks, blood slides and noir-style voice-overs, and whose humanity shows in the need to have his account of himself heard and corrected by another.

samples.book: 157 - Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy - Read and Gain Advantage on All Wisdom Checks
samples.title: Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy
samples.relation: Silcox's fifth-level paladin died to eighty-three orcs and his middle-school friends held a funeral, and the chapter asks whether grief for a PC death is rational. Charles Taylor's narrative ethics — we grasp our lives as unfolding stories — would vindicate it, but objections from Beckett's Waiting for Godot and MacEwan's Atonement (via critic Samantha Vice) show stories can discourage seeing life as narrative, and the decisive asymmetry is Nagel's point about death: after the paladin falls the campaign story continues and the player can still watch it, whereas a person's own death forecloses any finding out how things turn out, a difference like February cold versus interstellar cold. He proposes instead that the self is a 'back-story' or metanarrative precondition of storytelling, closing against Descartes' Meditations claim that the power of imagination is 'in no way necessary' to his essence — take away someone's capacity for shared fiction entirely and nothing recognizable remains.

samples.book: 141 - Avatar_ The Last Airbender and Philosophy - Wisdom from Aang to Zuko
samples.title: The Proud Disabled Person as Counterstory
samples.relation: Argues that Toph Beifong is not the harmful 'Supercrip' stereotype (an exceptional individual who overcomes disability through talent and grit, which blames ordinary disabled people for their disadvantage) but a 'Proud Disabled Person' counterstory. Her blindness is a disability gain: it led her to learn earthbending from the badgermoles, the original earthbenders, and to live immersed in bending as her constant way of navigating the world, deepening her mastery. Using Hilde Lindemann's master narratives and counterstories and Elizabeth Barnes's mere-difference view, the chapter shows Toph fits neither the 'better off dead' nor the 'irrationally happy' stereotype: she is grumpy, nuanced (adapting her teaching of Aang in 'Bitter Work'), and a central driver of the plot rather than a moral prop. Fricker's hermeneutical injustice explains why disabled viewers struggle to make sense of flourishing with a disability, and why Toph's portrait gives them permission to celebrate it.

samples.book: 122 - Westworld and Philosophy - Mind Equals Blown
samples.title: “I Always Felt this Place was Missing a Real Villain. Hence, My Humble Contribution.”
samples.relation: Eberl asks whether living out Sizemore-style fantasies can reveal or only corrode character: applying Aristotle's account of virtues and vices as habituated dispositions, he argues William's three decades in the park habituated the vices that made him the Man in Black — the park reveals rather than suspends the self — while cruelty toward humanlike hosts hardens us toward people, as Aquinas and Kant warn about kindness to animals. Against Ford's claim that humans are wantons in tight loops, Maeve's editing of her own code after learning her escape was scripted makes her a Frankfurtian person who aligns first-order desires with second-order volitions, grounding her narrative identity and personhood. William too attains personhood by actualizing a second-order desire for a different life, with the hosts' free fight back evoking Nietzsche's will to power and Nozick's point that we want to actually do things, not merely experience them.

samples.book: 031 - Johnny Cash and Philosophy - The Burning Ring of Truth
samples.title: A Modest Conclusion
samples.relation: Lindahl-Urben and Taliaferro stage the diachronic-versus-episodic debate about the self (Galen Strawson's episodic view included) against Leigh Edwards's "no single Johnny Cash": the hotel-room-wrecking addict and the Billy Graham touring Christian do not fit one biography. They argue the private J.R. was a third option: on stage he becomes wholly absorbed in story characters (the Folsom narrator, the man who shot a man in Reno) while a self not defined by time slips in and out of the persona, evidenced by his account of gradually shedding "Johnny Cash" after shows. Johnny Cash the public quilt is compared to the Ship of Theseus, every original piece of J.R. replaced yet still owned by him, and the modest conclusion is that J.R., like anyone making a free choice, stood above the timeline of instants and could inhabit both the episodes and the grand narrative.

samples.book: 056 - Dune and Philosophy - Weirding Way of the Mentat
samples.title: Long-Term Identity
samples.relation: Asks whether the final Duncan Idaho ghola, whose serial memories wake during his encounter with Murbella, is the same person as the original who died holding off nineteen Sardaukar. It tests physical continuity, Locke's memory-based sameness of person (Hayt becomes Duncan only when the original's consciousness reawakens), Parfit's psychological connectedness with its redescription of identity as survival through quasi-memory, Schechtman's narrative self-constitution, Velleman's self-inventing characters, and four-dimensionalist 'space-time worms' on which Leto II's 3,500 years and the Duncans' gappy five millennia are single long selves. Herbert's moral: identity is not fixed—societies and technologies, from the Tleilaxu tanks to the Sisterhood's swift accommodation, keep redrawing what counts as the same person. Same Duncans, same person.

samples.book: 033 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Mission Accomplished or Mission Frakked Up_
samples.title: Retelling Our Stories
samples.relation: Milsky uses Ricoeur and MacIntyre's narrative theory of personal identity to read the two Sharons: Boomer's fabricated human backstory suffers a 'factual disruption' when she shoots Adama, while Athena's 'disruption of belief' comes from falling in love with Helo. He argues such disruptions — also suffered by humans like Starbuck (recovered memories of abuse in 'Maelstrom'), Roslin (coming to believe she is Pythia's dying leader), and Helo — need not destroy identity, since narratives can be retold, as the Final Four do in 'Crossroads, Part 2' with Tigh's 'My name is Saul Tigh' speech. Third-party narratives (Six disowning Athena, the crew refusing to see Boomer as Boomer) show identity is partly socially constructed and can become self-fulfilling prophecy, with Boomer's blackouts resembling dissociative identity disorder.

samples.book: 038 - Radiohead and Philosophy - Fitter Happier More Deductive
samples.title: Where Pink Floyd Ends and Radiohead Begins
samples.relation: Reisch asks whether Radiohead is the Pink Floyd of the twenty-first century and answers that the comparison misleads: where Barrett-era Floyd used electronics to escape into psychedelic fantasy, Radiohead's apparent space-rock is phenomenological, giving voice to pre-reflective experience of technological modern life. He reads 'No Surprises' (Yorke singing with his head in a filling glass sphere) as a study in the political infantilization of commuters, and OK Computer's car crash ('Airbag'), 'Let Down', and 'Lucky' as registering the feel of a fragile, technology-saturated world. Quoting Marcuse's One-Dimensional Man and Chomsky on manufactured consent, he argues we can see no alternative to the technologically rational system, and then, against Descartes' priority of the isolated 'I', invokes Heidegger's Being-in-the-world and Merleau-Ponty's embodied subject to suggest that our deepening immersion in technology may be changing the self itself — the truth the collapsing pedestrians of the 'Just' video cannot face.

samples.book: 041 - Stephen Colbert and Philosophy - I Am Philosophy (And So Can You!)
samples.title: But Does Political Satire Promote Democratic Values
samples.relation: Michael Tiboris and Kory Schaff answer their title question affirmatively: Colbert's satire promotes democratic values by practicing Foucault's parrhesia - fearless speech that speaks the truth freely, functions as criticism of interlocutor and self, and flows from moral duty - unlike bumper-sticker assertion, since it enters risky dialogue and invites being refuted. Against this stands a corporate-consolidated media ('monopoly of meaning' from GE, Viacom, News Corp, Time-Warner) whose framing, slanting, and spinning - McCain's 'transcendental' war, the Obama-dresses-like-Ahmadinejad story, WMD as Word of the Year - exemplify Marcuse's one-dimensional thought absorbing oppositional language ('clean bomb,' 'harmless fall-out'). The WØRD models parrhesiastic critique by speaking media's own language while the bullet points undercut it ('Definitions will greet us as liberators'), exposing how politicians and pundits merely appear truthful and teaching viewers their own duty of critical assessment.

samples.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
samples.title: 40. Deadpool as Philosophy Using Humor to Rebel Against the System
samples.relation: Brake argues that Deadpool advances an implicit thesis about humor as a threefold vehicle of liberation, testing it against Horkheimer and Adorno's Frankfurt School charge that the culture industry produces interchangeable, aesthetically impoverished pop-culture 'trash' (the formulaic MCU) that pacifies workers, and Marcuse's warning that revolutionary material gets absorbed as just another commodity. Following Kathryn Tanner's rejoinder that consumers can creatively repurpose pop culture, he shows Wade Wilson's self-mocking, fourth-wall-breaking humor achieving personal liberation from tragedy (invoking Freud on humor as the ego's assertion of invulnerability), liberation from the oppressive Mutant Factory by exposing Ajax/Francis's vulnerability and asserting his own autonomy, and a partial liberation from superhero genre tropes, while conceding humor's reactionary tendency to reinforce the status quo since Deadpool ultimately reproduces the genre and hands Disney its money.

samples.book: 032 - Bruce Springsteen and Philosophy - Darkness on the Edge of Truth
samples.title: Springsteen’s Revolution
samples.relation: Anderson and Anderson open with the Che Guevara t-shirt problem and Marcuse's one-dimensional man: the system assimilates protest, so internal critique (Springsteen on the cover of Rolling Stone, its Chevrolet calendar, the Eagles sold at Wal-Mart, Adorno's verdict on co-opted popular music) is a sop to Cerberus. Against this they set Springsteen's own account of his music as 'a very long conversation with my audience' — a transactional public service — and argue he survives the co-optation charge as a 'Socratic revolutionary' who, like Socrates refusing to leave Athens, works from within: listening without obeying ('I liked the old Bruce better'), refusing to ride the Born to Run wave, turning to Guthrie and Seeger, and drawing no hard conclusions, only opening spaces of reflection ('Born in the U.S.A.', 'Radio Nowhere', 'Long Walk Home'). Revolution is just another form of work — practice, sweat, and the personal job of 'growin' up.'

samples.book: 182 - Mad Men and Philosophy - Nothing Is as It Seems
samples.title: Television and Existential Awakening
samples.relation: Jaarsma argues Mad Men dramatizes an existential rather than Kantian-enlightenment model of advertising: Don's 'freedom from fear' pitch ('Whatever you are doing is okay. You are okay') sells escape from the anxiety of real choice, which is precisely Sartrean bad faith and what de Beauvoir calls the stagnant 'happiness' of women rewarded for being the other. Betty on her psychiatrist's couch, Peggy measured by Joan's paper-bag mirror and the Playtex bullet-bra silhouette, and the closeted Salvatore all internalize the dominant values Marcuse describes, finding meaning in conformity to the objectifying gaze ('bras are for men; women want to see themselves the way men see them'). Rachel Menken, who refuses to 'put on an apron' and calls out the contingency of gendered embodiment, models authenticity as choosing to choose, and the chapter closes with the hope that television itself can occasion the viewer's existential awakening.

samples.book: 088 - Justified and Philosophy - Shoot First, Think Later
samples.title: Justified and Philosophy
samples.relation: The chapter argues coal made Boyd Crowder possible: company scrip, Bloody Harlan's union-busting terror, black lung (Boyd's would-be assassin takes the bridge job because mining ruined his lungs), and Black Pike's mountaintop removal leave Harlan no viable work outside the mines, so crime is the rational alternative. It reads this through Hegel's 'rabble' from the Philosophy of Right - civil society is never wealthy enough to prevent an excess of poverty, and the rabble loses the honor of self-support - plus Marcuse's affluent-society critique of an existence that 'violently defends its own servitude'. Boyd's outlawry, which sets its own code above mere criminality, is a rebellion against being pushed into the rabble, and Hegel's remedy of emigration explains why leaving Harlan is the only escape, though the coal train hauls coal out while the people stay.

samples.book: 107 - Deadpool and Philosophy - My Common Sense Is Tingling
samples.title: 3. The Only Chapter in This Book You Need to Read!
samples.relation: Writing as two bickering versions of himself from different universes, Karavitis reads Deadpool Kills Deadpool as showing that the multiverse of Deadpools is the delusion of a single narcissist: the alternate 'Pools' are mirror-image projections of himself (Lacan's mirror stage), his self-love is Rousseau's pathological amour propre rather than healthy amour de soi, and his claim to be the progenitor of all reality is solipsism—hence there is no fourth wall. Freud, Fromm, and Marcuse supply rival diagnoses of that narcissism, from arrested development to proto-fascist willfulness to authentic rebellion against social control through unconscious conformity. A closing twist argues philosophers who claim sole access to truth are the same solipsistic narcissists, which would make Socrates, who never claimed a final answer, the only true philosopher.

samples.book: 028 - The Grateful Dead and Philosophy - Getting High Minded about Love and Haight
samples.title: Forgetting the Love We Bring
samples.relation: John Drabinski argues that the Deadhead parking lot is an 'occasional community' offering real hope against modernity's managed, one-dimensional life. Starting from his own Amherst-to-Worcester commuter routine read through Wittgenstein's forms of life — a community of nodding strangers at the same mini-marts — he stages Marcuse's One-Dimensional Man and Bauman's managed death as the deadening background against which such moments crack open. Where the commuter's community stays merely occasional, the parking lot's saturated friendship and shared undergoing (com-passion, good trip and bad, frat guy comforting and comforted) converts occasion into a genuine alternative ethos, drawing on Heidegger's sense of ethos as dwelling place — an everyday miracle of conversion he says we need now more than ever.

samples.book: 024 - Bullshit and Philosophy - Guaranteed to Get Perfect Results Every Time
samples.title: Our Distinguished Panel of Incomparable Geniuses
samples.relation: Fuller's finale casts Francis Bacon's scientific method as an inquisitorial trial designed to manage bullshit: everyone may produce it, provided a third-party judge frames a 'crucial experiment' that decides between the parties — a vision only partially realized by the Royal Society and later positivism, and tempered by Karl Popper's open-society point that all may bullshit to their heart's content given agreement on how to clean up after it. He tests the model on the Lomborg affair (initially found 'scientifically dishonest', then acquitted on appeal because politicized research is the environmental norm), on Zola's J'Accuse and Galileo's vindication in Newton's Principia as productive bullshit, and on his own service as expert witness: McLean v. Arkansas cut through creationist and evolutionist bullshit with a neutral definition of science, while Kitzmiller v. Dover adopted a 'methodological naturalism' custom-built to exclude Intelligent Design — justice losing out to the side whose bullshit is piled higher and deeper.

samples.book: 075 - Psych and Philosophy - Some Dark Juju-Magumbo
samples.title: Psych and Philosophy
samples.relation: Stephenson tests Shawn's ruse against the major theories of justified deceit and finds it wanting: Plato's Myth of the Metals excuses paternalistic noble lies for social harmony that Shawn's self-aggrandizing motives cannot claim, utilitarianism collapses on the long-term costs of exposure (Gus, Juliet, Henry, and the SBPD condemned by association; clients betrayed; trust in law enforcement eroded), Kant's universalizability test sinks maxims like 'lie whenever a career opportunity is at stake,' and Popper's open society condemns just the deceit on which the psychic brand runs. Even the mutual-deceit analogy to poker and Sissela Bok's reasonable-person publicity test fail, since no public forum of reasonable people would bless duping paying private clients. The escape is extra-moral: Shawn's mischievous hokum is the socially necessary boundary-pusher, whose lesson against unreflective occult belief lands best when delivered with a laugh.

samples.book: 188 - The Ultimate South Park and Philosophy - Respect My Philosophah!
samples.title: THE ULTIMATE SOUTH PARK AND PHILOSOPHY
samples.relation: Argues that South Park performs Popper's defense of the open society by ridiculing 'enemies' on both flanks: Cartman as a Glenn Beck-style ranter in 'Dances with Smurfs' and a xenophobic border agent in 'The Last of the Meheecans', versus liberal fanatics like Rob Reiner in 'Butt Out', Rosie O'Donnell's recount antics in 'Trapper Keeper', and Tom Cruise's litigious Scientology in 'Trapped in the Closet'. The show does not silence extremists but lets them speak and then mocks them, which the authors read through Popper's paradox of tolerance: tolerance cannot be extended to those who suppress criticism, as the Church of Scientology's pressure campaigns showed. A closing section links this to Jefferson's Virginia Bill for Establishing Religious Freedom — 'truth is great and will prevail if left to herself' — making free, offensive argument and dissent the lifeblood of democracy.

samples.book: 116 - 1984 and Philosophy - Is Resistance Futile
samples.title: 7. Big Brother, We’re Watching You!
samples.relation: Tännsjö argues mass surveillance is here to stay, and since absolute privacy is technically impossible while targeted surveillance only stigmatizes the dissidents who most need protection, we should embrace reciprocal mass surveillance: radical transparency in which citizens can 'watch Big Brother back', secret-service records are opened, and whistleblowers like Snowden and Manning are honored as heroes. On the way he dismantles the standard defenses of privacy, including the honor-based right to control one's image, moral rights (following Thomson's denial of a distinct right to privacy), and dignity-based autonomy arguments, while conceding through Nagel and Rachels what would be lost if inner thoughts became readable. Winston's opening wish to see Big Brother as Big Brother sees him becomes the chapter's model of an open surveillance society.

samples.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
samples.title: 28. South Park as Philosophy Blasphemy, Mockery, and (Absolute ) Freedom of Speech
samples.relation: The chapter argues, via the 'Cartoon Wars,' '200,' and '201' episodes, that South Park makes five arguments about free speech and evaluates each. Johnson defends the claims that catering to terrorist threats breeds more terrorism and that mockery is 'all or nothing,' but rejects South Park's implied case for absolute free speech: using Mill's On Liberty and harm principle he shows the 'marketplace of ideas' fails (citing 8kun and Fox News), and using Popper's paradox of tolerance he argues intolerance cannot itself be tolerated. He proposes a middle-ground 'PC Principle' where society, not the state, curbs harmful speech through deplatforming and public shaming while distinguishing tolerance from acceptance.

samples.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
samples.title: Who Deceives Us
samples.relation: Defines the conspiracy through Cohaagen's team — Lori, Harry, Benny, and the turncoat Hauser — with the Adjustment Bureau as 'the quintessential conspiracy' claiming good consequences for humanity. Popper's argument that belief in efficient grand conspiracies is irrational (his 'cock-up theory of society') is tested against the Bureau's own bungled coffee spill that lets David meet Elise, while Keeley's Hume-style critique and the specter of unbridled skepticism about spouses, friends, and memories frame what it would cost to believe in such conspiracies.

samples.book: 181 - Ultimate Lost and Philosophy - Think Together, Die Alone
samples.title: NOTES
samples.relation: Davies treats the beach camp as an actual state of nature: the stolen drinking water is a tragedy of the commons, Shannon's inhalers show how the crash scrubs pre-existing property rights (Hobbes: two men desiring the same thing become enemies), and Jack and Sayid's torture of Sawyer marks the first step toward Locke's civil society by enforcing others' rights through punishment rather than self-defense. He rejects theories of human nature - Rousseauan 'Innocence' versus a 'Trust No One' outlook - in favor of the repeated prisoner's dilemma, arguing the survivors stabilize cooperation through tit-for-tat: beginning cooperative with strangers and retaliating against the Others. On this reading the real difference between Hobbes and Locke is which round of the repeated dilemma each takes as the starting point.

samples.book: 029 - Quentin Tarantino and Philosophy - How to Philosophize with a Pair of Pliers and a Blowtorch
samples.title: Don’t Get Into One
samples.relation: Richard Greene renames the Tarantino standoff the 'ex-convict's dilemma' and models it as a special case of the prisoner's dilemma, running from Ordell and Louis's separate interrogation rooms to the White–Pink, Joe–White–Eddie and True Romance shoot-outs. He argues the standard group-rationality solution fails because ECDS participants have conflicting goals—Eddie protecting his father, White protecting Orange, Joe wanting revenge—and his survey of Tarantino's six cases shows escapes come from luck (Mr. Blonde's entrance, Nikki coming home) or shared interests (Beatrix's pregnancy), never group rationality. Tracing the dilemma back to Glaucon's contract argument in Plato's Republic, he concludes the only reliable solution is: don't get into one.

samples.book: 026 - South Park and Philosophy - Bigger, Longer, and More Penetrating
samples.title: Gaining Trust from the Past
samples.relation: Richard Davies treats the Oceanic 815 survivors' beach as a "framed" state of nature: the stolen water is a tragedy of the commons, Sawyer's "finders keepers" defense of Shannon's inhalers stages Hobbes's war of all against all against Locke's natural rights, and Jack and Sayid's torture of Sawyer marks the first step toward civil society, a claim to punish on another's behalf. He argues no theory of human nature (Rousseau's "Innocence" versus a "Trust No. 1" attitude) is needed to understand the castaways: cooperation grows through iterated prisoner's-dilemma tit-for-tat strategies, which also recasts the real difference between Hobbesian and Lockean states of nature.

samples.book: 092 - Orange Is the New Black and Philosophy - Last Exit from Litchfield
samples.title: Orange Is the New Black and Philosophy
samples.relation: Greene reconstructs the Prisoner's Dilemma with Pennsatucky and Vee in separate interrogation rooms, then maps a variant onto 'Thirsty Bird': whatever Alex does, Piper is better off testifying against Kubra, yet mutual silence was the group-rational outcome the two pact on the van ride. Alex defects anyway, leaving Piper with perjury and no leniency, and Greene argues Piper should have done the 'rational' thing, since Balik's revenge is only a threat while extra time in Litchfield is a certain harm and Alex has always been willing to screw her. The episode shows why honor among the self-interested fails without trust.

samples.book: 030 - Pink Floyd and Philosophy - Careful with that Axiom, Eugene!
samples.title: Wondering and Dreaming. The Words Have Different Meanings
samples.relation: Scott Calef argues that the causal theory of perception — the inflatable pig over Battersea reaches you only as an internal representation — breeds Cartesian skepticism: the dreaming argument, asylum inmates who don't know they're mad ('the lunatic is in my head'), the evil demon, and the modern brain-in-a-vat version behind The Matrix. Locke's unknowable substratum behind the Dark Side jacket's qualities and Berkeley's idealism deepen the veil of perception, with 'Julia Dream', Waters's 'If I go insane, please don't stick your wires in my brain', and Syd's 'Jugband Blues' self-diagnosis as Floyd illustrations. Against skepticism he deploys mutual corroboration ('It takes two to know'), J.L. Austin's point that waking experience is qualitatively unlike dreams ('A Pillow of Winds': 'the dream is gone'), and Wittgenstein's beetle-in-a-box private language argument (rebranded as Lucifer Sam's cat) — a purely private language is impossible, so skepticism expressed in language defeats itself, leaving the Barrett-era enigma to keep philosophy's original wonder alive.

samples.book: 196 - Terminator and Philosophy - I'll Be Back, Therefore I Am
samples.title: NOTES
samples.relation: Peter Fosl asks what John Connor should do when the radio call comes from Crystal Peak — accept near-certain death leading the resistance or stay silent — and dismantles the easy answers: John is not the indispensable savior (Kate or the caller from Montana could lead), the flag-waving finale undercuts any claim that humanity deserves saving, and collective responsibility for Judgment Day is unjust. Social contract fails because Brewster's button-press dissolved the contract and returned humanity to Hobbes's and Locke's state of nature, Hume shows contracts cannot ground society, and utilitarianism wavers once the happiness of animals and possible-happy machines is counted. The positive argument extends Wittgenstein's private-language argument (via Stanley Cavell): meaningful existence is inescapably social and moral, so refusing the claims of others would be as self-subverting as a solipsist arguing in language, and John must answer the call to remain human at all.

samples.book: 098 - The Princess Bride and Philosophy - Inconceivable!
samples.title: 5. Does It Mean What Vizzini Thinks It Means
samples.relation: Fetterman takes Inigo's 'I do not think it means what you think it means' seriously and defends Vizzini: the line may merely record that two speakers define 'inconceivable' differently, or react to it differently. Using Wittgenstein, he argues communication requires agreement in judgments, so Vizzini and Inigo may simply be playing different language games, like users of two different dictionaries. He then runs Wittgenstein's private language argument against the possibility that Vizzini's usage is correct by his own idiosyncratic rules - a purely private definition could never be confirmed or be wrong, since only Vizzini checks it - and touches on the philosophical sense of 'conceivable' as logically possible (the square circle) and the group language game that lets everyone accept Miracle Max's 'to blave.'

samples.book: 137 - Alice in Wonderland and Philosophy - Curiouser and Curiouser
samples.title: Grand Masters of the Universe
samples.relation: Chases Cold War nuclear strategists down the rabbit-hole, reading the Mad Tea Party as the MAD (mutually assured destruction) tea party where 'to reduce the risk of nuclear war, the risk must be increased' passes for wisdom. Ron Hirschbein uses Wittgenstein's language games (Alice was his favorite English prose), Rorty's final vocabulary, and Derrida's remark that a nuclear war has never 'taken place' to argue that Nukespeak, deterrence, the 'Delicate Balance of Terror', and the post hoc ergo propter hoc argument for deterrence are ungrounded, unfalsifiable word games. The Queen of Hearts's 'Off with his head!' prefigures decapitation strategy and the Hitler card, and the looking-glass chessboard becomes the arms race in which the public are expendable pawns.

samples.book: 230 - The Philosophy of Spike Lee
samples.title: (Still) Fighting the Power Public Space and the Unspeakable Privacy of the Other in Do the Right Thing
samples.relation: Finnegan reads Do the Right Thing as a dramatization of philosophical skepticism and the 'problem of other minds,' using Wittgenstein's private-language argument, Austin's speech acts, and Cavell to argue that racism is not an epistemic failure to 'know' the Other but an ethical refusal to acknowledge. She shows Lee's split cinematic style (naturalistic interiority for the Italian Americans, alienating canted wide-angle shots for Radio Raheem and the black characters) enacts what being 'othered' looks like, while the Racial Slur Montage stages words as perlocutionary acts and Arendt's 'space of appearances' explains the black characters' exclusion. Mookie's thrown trash can and Sal's Wall of Fame register powerlessness rather than resolution.

samples.book: 216 - The Philosophy of Charlie Kaufman
samples.title: The Instructive Impossibility of Being John Malkovich
samples.relation: Hagberg treats Being John Malkovich as a refutation of the dualist fantasy that one could achieve transparent knowledge of another mind by occupying it. Through the film's four levels—Schwartz as spectator inside Malkovich, Lotte's transgender re-embodiment, Schwartz's puppeteering, and Malkovich falling into his own portal to the 'Malkovich, Malkovich' hell—he shows, via Jamesian relational sensation and Wittgenstein's private-language argument, that it is always still Schwartz who senses, so no one ever becomes Malkovich. The self-enclosed Malkovich world, where everyone can only say 'Malkovich,' dramatizes that selfhood is relationally emergent (Royce, Mead) and that experience is inviolably one's own (Margalit on remembered emotion).

samples.book: 274 - Coffee – Philosophy for Everyone - Grounds for Debate
samples.title: Coffee - Philosophy for Everyone
samples.relation: Sadler argues black coffee, unlike ceremonial tea, is the realist emblem of our anxious, isolated postmodern condition, and that the chain coffeehouse is a 'non-place' of public anonymity that only simulates the sociality we crave. Against Aristotle's confident view of humans as social animals whose eudaimonia presupposes a settled social order, she sets Nietzsche's alienated individual free to create values — then argues Nietzsche errs: using the trivial cappuccino-vs-latte choice, she shows (via Wittgenstein's private-language argument and Korsgaard) that even solitary choices need reasons intelligible to others, so individual choice cannot be self-justifying and our search for meaningful, non-arbitrary lives is irreducibly social.

samples.book: 113 - Jimi Hendrix and Philosophy - Experience Required
samples.title: 12. The Broken Pieces of Yesterday’s Life
samples.relation: Uses the flood of posthumous Hendrix releases — the dismal Lonnie Youngblood eight-track, 380-plus albums, the PPX litigations — to ask what we owe the dead and what access we may claim, weighing Kafka and Max Brod, Nietzsche's sister, Harper Lee's Go Set a Watchman, and Kundera's Mirek. It rejects the framing of conflicting rights: against the Cartesian picture of a hidden self the authors deploy Wittgenstein's beetle in the box — 'the human body is the best picture of the human soul' — to show that no one can fully control their public self, leaving only prudential discernment about which recordings should shape our image of the artist.

samples.book: 168 - Heroes and Philosophy - Buy the Book, Save the World
samples.title: NOTES
samples.relation: Distinguishes Matt Parkman's supernatural telepathy from the 'mundane mind reading' everyone performs, then argues even Matt's power cannot solve the problem of other minds: the suicidal woman's thoughts he hears in the bar ('One Giant Leap') could be part of a Maury-Parkman-style illusion, and a brain-to-brain link could never rule out that others are Chalmers-style philosophical zombies. After grounding the skepticism in Descartes' cogito and method of doubt, it defends our everyday attribution of minds by analogy (Audrey Hanson reading Claire's insincerity) on pragmatic grounds, and maps Matt's progression from hearing thoughts to nightmare manipulation and compulsion onto the four adaptive functions philosophers assign to mind reading: interpretation, prediction, coordination, and influence. It closes by showing why neuroimaging-based technological mind reading remains a pipe dream, since brain recordings are quantitative syntax without semantics.

samples.book: 074 - Planet of the Apes and Philosophy - Great Apes Think Alike
samples.title: Planet of the Apes and Philosophy
samples.relation: Kristin Andrews uses Taylor's silent attempts to show Zira he has a mind - mouthing answers, wiggling his fingers when she mentions the Hopkins Manual Dexterity Test - to stage the problem of other minds, pushing against Descartes's claim that language is required for thought and Mill's argument from analogy, while Dr. Zaius can always redescribe it all as 'a definite gift for mimicry.' Drawing on her fieldwork with the orangutan Cecep (the leaf-wiping pantomime, guiding the frightened Aldrin home from the turtle scare), she argues against reducing mindreading to false-belief tasks and for knowing minds through shared interaction, inductive overhypotheses, and natural context. She ends with an extended-mind point - 'when you're in a cage, you act caged,' and we offload thinking onto our homes and tools - so lab studies can show what apes can do but never what they can't.

samples.book: 054 - The Onion and Philosophy - Fake News Story True, Alleges Indignant Area Professor
samples.title: Point-Counterpoint Funny versus Really, Really Funny
samples.relation: Andrew Terjesen starts from real cases of Onion satire taken literally — a Michigan sheriff warning about al-Qaida telemarketing, the Beijing Evening News plagiarizing 'Congress Threatens To Leave D.C.', Deborah Norville reporting that 58 percent of American exercise is televised — and explains them through the Problem of Other Minds. Descartes' hats-and-cloaks worry and Russell's analogy solution show how we infer that a straight-faced writer is 'just kidding,' but the analogy fails when cultural context, prejudice (Fred Phelps citing the gay-recruitment story, Christians forwarding the Harry Potter Satanism piece), or wishful thinking breaks the comparison with our own joking behavior. The upshot is that humor is engineered misunderstanding — the Onion works by analogy to real news, and could never warn readers off without destroying the joke.

samples.book: 027 - Hitchcock and Philosophy - Dial M for Metaphysics
samples.title: Marnie An Enigma to Herself
samples.relation: Yanal sets Descartes's two claims about mind - certainty about one's own thoughts (via the method of doubt and the deceiving-evil-genius possibility) and skepticism about other minds (hats and coats that may cover automata) - against Wittgenstein's counters, then reads Shadow of a Doubt and Marnie as Hitchcock's counterexamples. In Shadow of a Doubt the two Charlies, twins in blood and in the film's doubling motifs, are 'transparent' to each other - Young Charlie alone knows her uncle is the Merry Widow Murderer - refuting other-minds skepticism; in Marnie, repressed memory of killing her mother's sailor client leaves Marnie ignorant of her own mind until Mark's amateur therapy recovers it, refuting Cartesian self-certainty. Both films thus side with Wittgenstein: one person can know another's mind, and one can be an enigma to oneself.

samples.book: 040 - Transformers and Philosophy - More than Meets the Mind
samples.title: Transformers and Philosophy
samples.relation: Pike asks what the All Spark's zap would have to do to give brought-to-life vending machines and steering wheels genuine minds, testing logical behaviorism's dispositions and Turing's conversation test against Searle's Chinese Room ('syntax is insufficient for semantics'), and weighing Descartes's God-given soul against physicalist alternatives: functionalism, Searle's biological naturalism, and reductive physicalism. Since we can never access another mind from the inside, he concludes that by abductive inference to the best explanation - Optimus Prime's mourning, planning, and moral decision-making being too complex for mere programming - we have as much reason to credit a Transformer with a mind as any human around us.

samples.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
samples.title: Empathy in a “More Human than Human” World
samples.relation: The chapter shows Deckard funding empathy for animals by killing androids, then raises the stakes: since android models keep improving, even close inspection of one's ostensibly 'real' sheep might fail to disclose a clever simulation, which it names as Dick's reconfiguration of the problem of other minds and solipsism. The desert toad, seen 'through Mercer's eyes' and boxed with painstaking care, is revealed by Iran to be electric, so that 'the desert of the real offers safe habitat only for virtual creatures.'

samples.book: 024 - Bullshit and Philosophy - Guaranteed to Get Perfect Results Every Time
samples.title: The Scientific Method as a Search for the Justice in Bullshit
samples.relation: Fuller portrays the bullshitter as the consummate hypocrite, bluffing from behind genuine uncertainty and exploiting the sophistic principle that controlling the moment of decision controls its outcome — calling the question when the balance of arguments favors you. Since we can rarely audit anyone's track record, epistemology leans on 'trust', 'witness' and 'testimony', read optimistically through Thomas Reid's divinely guaranteed common sense or, à la Kierkegaard, malignly as cowardly delegation of belief; either way 'reliability', which papers over the gap between evidence and belief, is itself a bullshit concept. He then analogizes the epistemic economy of evidence to the moral economy of sensation: as utilitarianism defers immediate gratification (taxation insuring against discounting our future selves), so the bullshitter's imperviousness to current evidence-weightings is prudence — an 'affirmative action' for weaker-evidenced positions that may prove the better bet in the fullness of time.

samples.book: 186 - Spider-Man and Philosophy - The Web of Inquiry
samples.title: Spider-Man and Philosophy
samples.relation: Terjesen uses spider-sense to tour early-modern philosophy of perception: against direct realism, Locke's indirect realism and its primary/secondary quality distinction suggest 'dangerousness' is a perceiver-relative secondary quality — bombs threaten Spider-Man but not the Hulk, and Mysterio manufactures danger-experiences — while Berkeley's idealism and Hume's phenomenalism radicalize the resulting skepticism about ever verifying sense data. The decisive clue is that spider-sense fails when Aunt May conks Peter with a vase (Amazing Spider-Man #114) and when his mentor Miles Warren becomes the Jackal: Peter does not fear those he loves. This supports Hume's sentimentalist account of moral judgment, on which vice is found not in the act but in the disapproving sentiment, moderated by Reid's common-sense reply that perception always already contains judgment — so spider-sense is a moralized judgment about what to avoid, not a Geiger counter.

samples.book: 075 - Psych and Philosophy - Some Dark Juju-Magumbo
samples.title: Psych and Philosophy
samples.relation: McCraw turns the question 'should we trust Shawn?' into the philosophy of testimony: Lassiter's policy of never believing without independent evidence embodies Hume's demand that testimony be backed by evidence of the speaker's reliability, while Buzz McNab's instant faith embodies Reid's innate principles of veracity and credulity, and both extremes fail the department - Lassiter solves too late, McNab chases every early false lead. Juliet's developing, flexible trust - suspicious at first, convinced by results, never naive - models the circumstantial middle path that no hard-and-fast Humean or Reidian rule can capture. The verdict: treat Shawn's testimony as both psychic and psychotic, trusting the track record in some cases and discounting the wilder 'visions' in others, because when to trust is unavoidably vague and case-by-case.

samples.book: 105 - The Ultimate Game of Thrones and Philosophy - You Think or Die
samples.title: 23. How Can We Know Anything in a World of Magic and Miracles
samples.relation: Baldwin asks whether Westerosi characters can know anything inductive in a world without lawlike nature: seasons of unpredictable length, wargs in animal minds, Faceless Men changing faces, and resurrections by Thoros, Melisandre, and Qyburn. After laying out the Platonic justified-true-belief analysis of knowledge (those who saw the pyre are justified in believing Dany is the mother of dragons; those relying on rumor are not), he runs Hume's problem of induction - we never perceive causal connection, so no jar of wildfire must explode - against Reid's common-sense reply that reason and induction stand or fall together, concluding that Westeros gives its people special reasons for skepticism while we, lacking evidence of magical irregularity, are rational to trust everyday inductive belief.

samples.book: 101 - Discworld and Philosophy - Reality Is Not What It Seems
samples.title: 8. Honesty Trumps Cleverness Sam Vimes and Commonsense Philosophy
samples.relation: Skene argues Sam Vimes embodies Thomas Reid's common sense philosophy across Feet of Clay, Thud!, Night Watch, and Jingo: he refuses speculation (his hatred of Holmes-style clue-deduction and the Summoning Dark), is irreverent toward false authorities from Sergeant Colon's 'School of My Dad Always Said' to Lord Rust's glorious wars, and checks every theory against reality. Moore's here-is-one-hand reply to Humean skepticism and Socrates' unmasking of pompous authorities illustrate the method, and Huemer's political realism - taxation as demanded money with menaces, social systems judged by how they work for real people - echoes Vimes's verdicts on Reg Shoe's utopian barricade and Swing's phrenology. The lesson is Vimes's own: 'Common sense and facts! That's what works.'

samples.relation: A chapter-length epistemology tutorial delivered as Cooper's tapes to Diane, applying the justified-true-belief analysis of knowledge to his investigation. The chapter cautions against confirming vague prophecies like bunny-shaped clouds, concluding Cooper becomes a truly "Special Epistemic Agent."

samples.book: 093 - More Doctor Who and Philosophy - Regeneration Time
samples.title: 9. How the Doctor Knows
samples.relation: Smithka argues the Doctor is a reliabilist about knowledge rather than a Cartesian strong foundationalist: using 'Amy's Choice,' 'The Beast Below' (the glass of water, the engine room, Amy's inference that the Star Whale came willingly), 'Silence in the Library' (the chicken-leg experiment implicating the Vashta Nerada), and Davros's Dalek trials in 'Genesis of the Daleks,' she shows him trusting perception in the right causal chain and reasoning inductively and abductively—Peirce's inference to the best explanation—instead of demanding Cartesian certainty. Against Descartes's dream and evil-genius skepticism, updated as Putnam-style brain-in-a-vat scenarios via the Dream Crabs of 'Last Christmas' and the Dream Lord's two-worlds game, she deploys Goldman's three criteria for perceptual knowledge: justification is packed into reliable belief-forming processes, and doubt is warranted only in known abnormal contexts like funhouses or Dream Lord games.

samples.book: 163 - Game of Thrones and Philosophy - Logic Cuts Deeper Than Swords
samples.title: Game of Thrones and Philosophy
samples.relation: Abraham Schwab turns Ygritte's 'You know nothing, Jon Snow' into a theory of epistemic humility: Jon misreads wildling courtship norms, Sam's dragonglass shatters on wight Small Paul, Lord Mormont assumes Mance fights like a southern king and pays for it at the Fist of First Men, while Arya's accurate self-knowledge keeps her alive. Formalizing with justified true belief - Sam's lucky dagger thrust is not knowledge, and the Watch's warranted belief that the dead Othor was harmless justifies falsity - he uses Lysa's letter, which sent Ned to King's Landing on a lie, to ask what justification is: Descartes's absolute certainty is too strict, reliabilism vindicates testimony ('dark wings, dark words'), so that only Sansa need witness Ned's beheading for the Starks to know it, and between Melisandre's circular dogma about Azor Ahai and total skepticism, moderate skepticism best governs belief - a humility the south lacked about the Horn of Winter.

samples.book: 058 - Dexter and Philosophy - Mind over Spatter
samples.title: More than a Feeling
samples.relation: Rachel Robison-Greene asks whether Dexter's rule to 'be sure' actually gives him knowledge of his victims' guilt. Distinguishing Cartesian certainty - skeptical hypotheses about deceiving senses, dreams and evil demons, echoing The Matrix - from mere felt certainty, she tests the belief-truth-justification analysis of knowledge traced to Plato against the show: LaGuerta's witness theory fails on belief, Deb's conviction that Neil Perry is the Ice Truck Killer fails on truth, and Astor's accusation of Dexter fails on justification. Neither strong internalism (Dexter straps down Jamie Jaworski without knowing how the murder was done), weak internalism, coherence theory (his false but coherent case against Jonathan Farrow), nor reliabilism (his spidey-sense is explicitly not sufficient by his own admission) captures his practice, so his 'certainty' is just a feeling - and the people on his table may include ones he does not know to be guilty.

samples.book: 075 - Psych and Philosophy - Some Dark Juju-Magumbo
samples.title: Psych and Philosophy
samples.relation: The Senors use Psych to separate true belief from knowledge: Shawn's hunch that Shabby the sea lion was murdered is true but shabbily evidenced, and his justified, true belief that a Clayton family member sabotaged the plane fails to be knowledge when the killer turns out to be a son-in-law he had no reason to think existed - a textbook Gettier case from 'He Dead.' They then weigh the two main theories of justification, evidentialism (with its base rates and prior probabilities) and reliabilism, and both vindicate the careful, methodical work of Lassiter and Juliet while Shawn's trigger-happy belief-forming habit strikes out twice. Shawn is redeemed only as an evidence-generator whose disregard for priors takes 'impossible' suspects like a murdered sea lion seriously, so that pairing his talents with the detectives' rigor yields the complete detective.
