Solomon Johnson asks whether Holmes's conclusions are knowledge or luck, walking through justified true belief with a Holmesian Gettier case (Watson rightly believing the killer was a former ship hand for the wrong reason), Moore's proof that knowledge entails belief, and Russell's stopped clock as an unsafe belief. BBC Sherlock's fake Vermeer and the 2009 film's 'resurrected' Lord Blackwood illustrate beliefs that fail safety or sensitivity across nearby possible worlds, while 'The Stock-Broker's Clerk' shows Holmes's observation of the scorched slippers making his belief sensitive. The verdict: Holmes is justified by the track record of his own expert methods, a professional billiards player rather than a beginner's-luck fluke, though real-world imitators could never rule out enough alternatives to match him.

samples.book: 068 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Zombie Apocalypse Now
samples.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
samples.relation: Richard Greene asks what, if anything, walkers know. Rick's optimistic feeling that Lori and Carl survived turns out true, yet is not knowledge - true belief is necessary but insufficient, the gap Gettier cases exploit - and since walkers can never weigh evidence or think about their thoughts, only externalist, reliability-based accounts of knowledge can count them as knowers. Walker behavior defeats Jenner's 'mindless instinct' line: Jenny turning the handle of her old house, the little girl walker retrieving her teddy bear, a walker smashing the department store window with a rock, and the horde seeing through Rick and Glenn's gut disguise once rain washes the scent away. Zombie knowledge is real but limited to simple things recalled from the person's past, the more complex the task the less likely they know it.

samples.book: 154 - Doctor Strange and Philosophy - The Other Book of Forbidden Knowledge
samples.title: A Strange Ending
samples.relation: Manninen applies virtue epistemology — built on Aristotle's virtue ethics and golden mean — to the four students of the Ancient One, asking not what they knew of the mystic arts but how they knew it. Strange's photographic memory exemplifies reliabilist epistemic ability, while Montmarquet's responsibilist virtues (impartiality, intellectual courage) are measured against Pangborn's self-serving magic, Kaecilius's courage without impartiality, and Mordo's epistemic rigidity and blind deference to authority ('no more questions'), each a vice of excess or deficiency. The Book of Cagliostro frames Wong's 'no knowledge in Kamar-Taj is forbidden, only certain practices,' and Strange emerges closest to the balanced intellectual character, though Aristotle demands consistency, not a single virtuous act.

samples.book: 122 - Westworld and Philosophy - Mind Equals Blown
samples.title: Violent Ends
samples.relation: Richards asks what it is like to be a host, combining three lenses: Searle's biological naturalism (thinking machines must be built from materials with the right causal powers, and the hosts' synthetic flesh may qualify), Nagel's bat (even if hosts are conscious, their perfectly relived memories, curated pain, and blind spots like 'it doesn't look like anything to me' may make their experience as inconceivable to us as echolocation), and Chalmers's philosophical zombies (hosts behave exactly like us, yet beings identical to them with no inner light are conceivable). He reads Ford's contradictory testimony — praising Bernard's guilt as 'a thing of beauty' while denying consciousness exists — as a shift to a deflationary view with no threshold for being alive, and argues the show's choice to film human and host experience in the same style keeps the question deliberately open while fostering empathy.

samples.book: 303 - Philosophy and the Interpretation of Pop Culture
samples.title: NOTES
samples.relation: Matthews argues that certain children's books are 'subversive' in a Socratic sense: they problematize concepts adults assume they command, challenging adult epistemic authority the way Socrates exposed the pretended knowledge of Athens' elite. Morris the Moose raises Aristotelian questions of natural kinds and essence-versus-accident; Leese Webster probes the concept of art; The Shrinking of Treehorn destabilizes 'normal' child development; Frog and Toad's 'The Garden' dramatizes the post hoc, ergo propter hoc fallacy about causation. In the Ozma of Oz Tik-Tok discussion, nine-year-old Paul reconstructs an argument that only brains think, which Matthews aligns with Searle's claim in The Mystery of Consciousness that consciousness is caused by specific neurobiological processes; he explicitly distinguishes his subversive stories from those promoting Pyrrhonian skepticism or Protagorean relativism.

samples.book: 035 - Star Trek and Philosophy - The Wrath of Kant
samples.title: “Logic Is the Beginning of Wisdom . . . Not the End”
samples.relation: Treats Kirk's computer-killing arguments as logic lessons: his valid syllogism forces Nomad to sterilize itself in 'The Changeling,' while the M-5's trial in 'The Ultimate Computer' models inductive hypothesis testing. The Liar paradox ('Everything Harry tells you is a lie' / 'I am lying') crashes Norman in 'I, Mudd' and, via Tarski's T-sentences and the explosion problem, reveals the concept of truth as inconsistent, with three-valued logic offered as a fix that only relocates the paradox. Gödel's incompleteness theorem then grounds the Lucas-Penrose claim that minds outstrip computer programs like Landru — which Putnam's consistency objection rebuts — leaving Searle's point that computers manipulate symbols without understanding them as the residue of Surak's Vulcan logic being the beginning of wisdom, not the end.

samples.book: 106 - Peanuts and Philosophy - You're a Wise Man, Charlie Brown!
samples.title: 7. Life, Liberty and the Pursuit of a Warm Blanket
samples.relation: The chapter explains Linus's blanket via Winnicott's transitional objects, then argues the gang's wider habits - Great Pumpkin taboos, baseball fetishes and rituals - are 'magical thinking' that manufactures an illusion of control over an uncertain world. A middle section tours the mind-body problem (Hippocrates, Descartes's dualism and pineal gland, Huxley's epiphenomenalism, Searle's emergent consciousness) to ask who is really doing the reading. The fallacies section dissects Linus's unfalsifiable Pumpkin doctrine (post hoc after the taboo-breaking 'if') and Charlie's confirmation bias, before reframing his 'pantophobia' as Kierkegaardian angst and Sartrean nausea: with adults reduced to 'Mwaa mwaa mwaa,' the kids are condemned to be free.

samples.book: 026 - South Park and Philosophy - Bigger, Longer, and More Penetrating
samples.title: The Role of Matter Biology or Function
samples.relation: Lawrence asks which theory of mind best fits the Matrix trilogy. Cartesian dualism (with its pineal-gland plug standing in for Neo's headjack) would explain Neo's jackless mind in the Train Station but lacks evidence and faces the interaction problem, so the chapter defends a fully materialist reading — Neo's sentinel-destroying signal and burnt-eye sight reconstrued as Matrix hardware in his skull. It then contrasts reductive and eliminative materialism, Searle's beer-can biological naturalism, and functionalism via Lewis's Martian pain, concluding that the films' sentient machines — Agent Smith's seamless copy into Bane's body — presuppose functionalism.

samples.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
samples.title: The Right Stuff
samples.relation: Applies Searle's Chinese Room to argue that functional equivalence alone would not make androids sentient, then observes that Dick's androids — biological 'chitinous reflex machines' detectable only by bone-marrow and Boneli reflex-arc tests, unlike obviously mechanical electric sheep — may possess the biological 'right stuff' Searle requires for intentional content. It closes by weighing this against the Turing/Dick behavioral view and the Wittgensteinian choice of which language game to play, calling the latter 'the most humanistic' reading.

samples.book: 182 - Mad Men and Philosophy - Nothing Is as It Seems
samples.title: Nonetheless, Don Can Be a Real Heel
samples.relation: Terjesen asks whether Don is a good man, testing his mixed record (egalitarian instincts, loyalty to Mohawk Airlines, protecting Horace Jr., against habitual adultery and the stolen identity) through Aristotle's habituation, Plato's Protagoras unity-of-virtues theses, Hume's sensible knave, and John Doris's situationist attack on global character traits. The unity theses imply Don's vices undermine his virtues (affairs make him unavailable when Betty crashes; evasions about his past block honesty), and Doris's dime-in-the-payphone literature suggests even Don's reliability may be circumstance-bound, as with Pete's weddings-and-vacations-only philandering. Against full situationism, Don's consistent rules (never forcing women, valuing women he genuinely finds interesting) point to 'regional' traits, yet Roger's verdict stands: 'You're no good with relationships because you don't value them,' since Don runs family on a business code, from Adam's bribe to 'that's what people do' consolation for Pete.

samples.book: 031 - Johnny Cash and Philosophy - The Burning Ring of Truth
samples.title: And Beware of the Beast in Me
samples.relation: Barnes takes Cash's infidelity despite the pledged fidelity of "I Walk the Line" and refuses the easy diagnoses of hypocrisy or lying: "Guess Things Happen that Way" voices a good will overcome by weakness, a frail human nature anyone shares. He supports this with the situationist experiments, the dime in the pay-phone slot, the Princeton seminarians in a hurry, Milgram's obedient schoolteachers, and the Stanford prison simulation that turned a pacifist student into an abusive guard, showing situation outweighs character. From Cash's songs he draws two moral lessons: charity toward wrongdoers, since the man in "I Never Picked Cotton" or the drunkard of "Kneeling Drunkard's Plea" might be us under the same circumstances, and prudence about compromising situations, as when Billy Joe's fatal pride in "Don't Take Your Guns to Town" proves his mother right.

samples.book: 285 - Serial Killers – Philosophy for Everyone - Being and Killing
samples.title: SERIAL KILLERS
samples.relation: Alfano uses the trial of 'Sunset Strip Killer' Doug Clark to argue that situational forces and attribution biases may have swayed his jury regardless of the actual evidence. Drawing on Milgram's obedience study, Zimbardo's prison simulation, Knobe's intentionality vignettes, and Haidt's disgust experiments, he shows how gender bias, pretrial media, and revulsion at Clark's necrophilia could distort judgments of guilt. He closes with Nozick's truth-tracking account of knowledge to press whether a juror who would have convicted anyway can be said to know Clark is guilty.

samples.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
samples.title: 34. The Lord of the Rings as Philosophy Environmental Enchantment and Resistance in Peter Jackson and J.R.R. T
samples.relation: Whitmire and Henderson read Peter Jackson's LotR films as environmental philosophy, arguing they use fantasy to recover a sense of nature's wonder and model a plurality of caring, non-instrumentalizing ways of inhabiting the land (Hobbits' gardens, the Rohirrim and their horses, the Elves of Lorien, the Ents of Fangorn) against the extractive, insatiable devastation of Saruman's Isengard and Sauron's Mordor. They explicitly deploy Leopold's Land Ethic ('the conqueror role is eventually self-defeating') to condemn Saruman's clear-cutting and dam-building, and Val Plumwood's ecofeminist notion of 'backgrounding' to explain why holding trees and mountains in visual focus is itself an argument. Thoreau's Maine Woods passage on the living pine grounds their claim that a tree is more than lumber, and the film's resistance (the Ents tearing out the dam, the White Tree's bloom) is read as a call to active ecological hope.

samples.book: 169 - The Hobbit and Philosophy - For When You've Lost Your Dwarves, Your Wizard, and Your Way
samples.title: a14.xhtml
samples.relation: Stewart argues Middle-earth magic is rule-bound engineering rather than Hume's miracle as 'a violation of the laws of nature': spells fail, the Ring hides neither shadow nor wet footprints, and magic comes in strengths like gravity, so fear of Gandalf is fear of superior knowledge of nature's laws, not of lawlessness. The deeper point is Tolkien's linkage of magic with technology as the impatient will to make one's will effective quickly - Sauron is 'Lord of magic and machines', the Ring is the supreme technological artifact, Saruman's forged men and blast-fires embody domination - while elvish 'Art' is sub-creation and Beorn's communion with animals models harmony with nature. Like Thoreau pricing possessions in 'how much life' they cost, the chapter ends with Tolkien's warning that 'if a thing can be done, it should be done' is the great false assumption of our age.

samples.book: 028 - The Grateful Dead and Philosophy - Getting High Minded about Love and Haight
samples.title: Dizzy with the Possibilities
samples.relation: Allen Thompson treats 'Throwing Stones' — 'the future's here, we are it, we are on our own' — as voicing the existential dread of anthropogenic global warming and the felt 'end of nature' Bill McKibben named, defending the song as the band's a-political polemic against heartless powers. He argues via Steven Vogel that humans cannot literally end nature unless we are supernatural, and recasts the crisis with Thoreau and Gary Snyder as civilization's assault on the wild, the self-willed order we too belong to. Deep ecology then supplies the response: re-identify the self as wild — as Deadheads do by dancing wildly to the music — and build a civilization wildness can endure, with the band's 1988 rainforest-benefit press conference as evidence of the Dead's own ecological consciousness.

samples.book: 082 - Jurassic Park and Philosophy - The Truth Is Terrifying
samples.title: Jurassic Park and Philosophy
samples.relation: Fitzpatrick argues that the awe Ellie feels at the brachiosaurs makes experiencing real dinosaurs so valuable that restoring them may be obligatory, and reads Malcolm's distrust of land managers as sharing Leopold's land ethic, under which firebombing Isla Nublar would be barbarism on the order of Dresden. Invoking Bentham, Mill, and Singer's expansion of the moral community (echoed in the park's dart guns), he weighs Elliot's 'Faking Nature' and Katz's charge that restored nature is a fake and an arrogance against Andrew Light's defense of respectful restoration. He concludes that Jurassic Park failed not because restoration is wrong but because Hammond restored dinosaurs for amusement, and that a careful, land-ethic-respecting de-extinction could one day be justified.

samples.book: 298 - The Philosophy of Tolkien - The Worldview Behind The Lord of the Rings
samples.title: The Lord of the Rings and Philosophy
samples.relation: Andrew Light resists reading the peoples of Middle-earth as simple stand-ins for parts of nature, noting that the ents, not the elves, truly speak for the forest, so nature is animated to stand and speak for itself. His central idea is 'green time': through Tom Bombadil and the ents, Tolkien represents a naturally scaled, ecosystemic, near-indifferent temporal perspective, seen when Bombadil is unconcerned with the Ring and the ents ignore the riders of Rohan. Light argues this indifference should not make us indifferent to nature but should teach humility and long-term responsibility for problems like global warming, imagining what it is to care for things as a process beyond our own lifespan.

samples.book: 114 - American Horror Story and Philosophy - Life Is But a Nightmare
samples.title: 15. Red Harvest in Roanoke
samples.relation: Reads Roanoke through ecocriticism and ecofeminism: the culture-nature dualism collapses as the urban Millers' wooded retreat turns predatory (rain of teeth, pig-men); the Butcher's backstory - a colonial woman starved by men whose blood-sacrifice pact makes the land flourish - aligns women and Nature as co-exploited by patriarchy, with Shelby's 'irrational' warnings ignored and Lee's maternal fury a force of nature; the animalizing of victims (pig-headed roasting, the Polks' barn-raised children, Matt's tryst with the Witch of the Wood) dissolves the human/animal hierarchy; and the media crew's attempt to package wilderness for ratings ends with Nature striking back at Agnes in the woods.

samples.book: 060 - SpongeBob SquarePants and Philosophy - Soaking Up Secrets Under the Sea!
samples.title: Friends—Don’t Leave Home without ’Em
samples.relation: Greg Ahrenhoerster places SpongeBob in literary history between Transcendentalism and naturalism: 'Nature Pants' is a failed Walden — SpongeBob gives away his possessions for Jellyfish Fields but his 'jellyfish instincts' fail as badly as self-reliance in London's 'To Build a Fire' — while 'Squidville' shows the industrial city's cold indifference as in Crane's Maggie. 'Jellyfish Hunter' warns that trying to exploit nature (Krabs's jelly factory) invites nature's reprisal, since civilized beings without instinct are at nature's mercy. The naturalist moral, against Transcendentalist solitude, is that we survive only through each other: visit Jellyfish Fields, but bring a friend.

samples.book: 262 - Dr. Seuss and Philosophy - Oh, the Thinks You Can Think!
samples.title: Speaking for Business, Speaking for Trees Business and Environment in The Lorax
samples.relation: The Klaassens read The Lorax as a joint business-and-environmental-ethics text organized around three questions the Thneed provokes: do we consume too much (invoking Thoreau's 'simplify' and DesJardins on practical, ethical, and environmental over-consumption), must business grow (Daly's distinction between quantitative growth and qualitative development), and why the Once-ler ignores sustainability (the Brundtland definition and Daly's rules for natural capital). The Lorax's self-appointment as one who 'speaks for the trees' is tied to Christopher Stone's argument that natural objects should have legal standing through guardians, like corporations or incompetents.
